1.1: It was year thirty for me, fourth month, fifth day—I was chillin' with the other exiles by the Chebar River, when boom! The heavens cracked open and I saw somethin' straight divine.
1.2: This was in year five since King Jehoiachin got snatched up. Mark that down.
1.3: That's when the word of the Lord came through loud and clear to me—Ezekiel, a priest, son of Buzi. We was in Babylonian land, by that same river. And right there, God laid His hand heavy on me.
1.4: I looked up—and whoa! A whirlwind came rushin' out the north. A big storm cloud, on fire from the inside, light shootin' out like it was burnin' gold, bright and wild in every direction.
1.5: In the middle of all that fire? Four strange-lookin' creatures. They had a human form… but they was definitely not human.
1.6: Each one had four faces and four wings.
1.7: Their legs was straight like poles, feet like calf hooves—but they shined like polished bronze. Straight gleamin'.
1.8: Under them wings? Human hands on all four sides. And every single one of these creatures had faces and wings.
1.9: Their wings touched each other—like they moved in sync. They ain't turn when they walked either. Nah, they moved straight ahead, like they was on assignment.
1.10: Now, these faces? Wild. Each had four: A human face upfront, A lion face on the right, An ox face on the left, And an eagle face on the back.
1.11: Their wings stretched up—two of 'em touched each other, two covered their bodies like cloaks.
1.12: And when they moved? They followed the Spirit. No hesitation, no detours. Just… straight where the Spirit said go.
1.13: These beings looked like they was made of fire—like coals glowin' and torches dancin'. Lightning flashed out from 'em, and they darted back and forth like bolts of light. Blink and you'd miss it.
1.14: They was movin' like ZOOM!—just a flash.
1.15: I peeped the ground near each creature and saw a wheel beside each one. And these wheels? Nah, not regular. They was something else.
1.16: The wheels looked like shimmering beryl stone. All four had the same setup—like a wheel inside another wheel, interlocked but free.
1.17: When they moved, they could shift in any direction, but still never turned. Just rolled wherever the Spirit said go.
1.18: The rims? So tall, they was intimidating. And the rims had eyes all around—watchin' everything. Every angle. Nothing got past 'em.
1.19: When the creatures moved, the wheels moved too. When they lifted up, the wheels lifted too.
1.20: Wherever the Spirit wanted to go, they went—and the wheels followed, because the Spirit of the creatures was in the wheels.
1.21: If the creatures moved, the wheels moved. If the creatures stopped, the wheels stopped. They was connected deep, spiritually synced.
1.22: Above their heads was somethin' like a dome—a vault of crystal, shiny and awe-inspiring, stretched out like the sky.
1.23: Underneath that dome, their wings spread out—two wings each touchin' another creature, two coverin' their own bodies.
1.24: When they flew, it sounded like roaring water, like God Himself was speakin'. Loud like an army rushin'. But when they stopped, the wings dropped silent.
1.25: Then I heard a voice—from above the dome that was over their heads.
1.26: And above that dome? A throne. It looked like it was carved from sapphire. And sittin' on that throne? A figure—a Man, high and lifted.
1.27: From the waist up, He glowed like molten metal, fire swirlin' all around. From the waist down? Fire again, with brilliance shootin' out like the sun.
1.28: The whole thing lit up like a rainbow on a rainy day—that's what the glory of the Lord looked like. When I saw it, I hit the ground. Face to the dirt. Couldn't even speak. And then I heard a voice… talkin' to me.

2.1: Then He told me, "Get up, son of man. Stand on your feet—I got somethin' to say to you."
2.2: Soon as He spoke, the Spirit filled me up and stood me upright. I could hear His voice, clear as day.
2.3: He said, "Listen up, son of man. I'm sendin' you to Israel—yeah, the whole nation. They wildin'. They been rebelled against Me for generations. This ain't new—they mama and daddy been actin' up too.
2.4: These folks hardheaded and got no shame. But I'm still sendin' you. And you gon' tell them straight up, 'This what the Lord God said.'
2.5: Whether they wanna listen or not—'cause trust, they some rebellious folks—they gon' know a real prophet done stepped in the room.
2.6: Now you, son of man, don't be scared of 'em. Don't let their words or their threats shake you. Even if you feel like you livin' in a field full of thorns, or chillin' with scorpions—still, don't be shook. Don't let they mean mugs or side-eyes faze you. They rebellious, yeah—but I still need you to speak.
2.7: You gon' say exactly what I tell you. Don't matter if they listen or not. Say it anyway. They need to hear it.
2.8: But listen—you, son of man, don't be like them. Don't rebel like they do. Open your mouth and eat what I give you."
2.9: Then I looked up—and saw a hand reachin' out to me. In it? A scroll. Like a heavenly book.
2.10: He opened it in front of me. Both sides was full of words—front and back. But it wasn't no happy story. Nah—it was full of sorrow, pain, and warnings. Grief on every line.

3.1: Then He told me, "Son of man, eat what I'm givin' you. This scroll right here—consume it. Then go speak to Israel."
3.2: So I opened my mouth, and He fed me that scroll Himself.
3.3: He said, "Fill your belly, son. Let this Word get down in your soul." I ate it, and no lie—it tasted sweet, like honey on my tongue.
3.4: Then He said, "Now go. Take these words I just gave you and speak 'em to Israel.
3.5: I ain't sendin' you to folks speakin' a foreign tongue or some language you can't decode. Nah—I'm sendin' you to your own people.
3.6: If I had sent you to another nation with unfamiliar speech, they'd probably listen. They would've paid attention.
3.7: But not Israel. They stubborn, hardheaded, and spiritually deaf. They don't listen to Me, so they won't listen to you either.
3.8: But don't trip—I made your face just as strong as theirs. Matter fact, stronger. Your forehead tougher than theirs.
3.9: I gave you a head like flint—like stone that can't be cracked. So don't be scared of they looks, don't be shook by they attitude. They still rebellious, but you built for this."
3.10: Then He told me, "Son of man, take all these words to heart. Lock 'em in. Listen close.
3.11: Then get up, go to your people in exile, and tell 'em, 'This what the Lord God said'—whether they down to listen or not."
3.12: Right then the Spirit lifted me up. And behind me I heard this loud voice like thunder yellin', "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from where He reigns!"
3.13: I also heard the sound of wings—the ones from them creatures—all clappin' together, and the wheels right next to 'em rumblin'. It was loud, like a storm hittin'.
3.14: The Spirit carried me off, and I was heated. Heart heavy, bitter spirit. But God's hand was holdin' me the whole way.
3.15: I got to Tel Abib, where the exiles stayed by the Chebar River. I sat with them in silence—shocked, overwhelmed—for seven whole days.
3.16: After them seven days, God spoke again:
3.17: "Son of man, I'm makin' you a watchman over Israel. That means you gotta listen when I speak, and then warn the people straight up.
3.18: If I say, 'This wicked person gon' die,' and you don't say nothin'—don't warn 'em, don't tell 'em to turn from their mess—they'll die in their sin. But you? I'll hold you accountable for that blood.
3.19: But if you do warn them and they still choose evil, they'll die in their own sin. But you? You off the hook. You did your part.
3.20: Now if a righteous person flips and starts wildin', and I put a trap in their path and you don't speak up? They gon' die too. And everything good they ever did? Wiped clean. And guess what? I'm holdin' you responsible.
3.21: But if you warn that righteous person not to slip up, and they listen? They gon' live. And you? You saved your own soul by speakin' up."
3.22: Then God's hand pressed on me again. He said, "Get up. Go out into the open plains—I got somethin' to tell you there."
3.23: So I went. And sure enough, the same glory I saw back at the Chebar River showed up again, heavy and radiant. I fell on my face.
3.24: Then the Spirit picked me up, stood me on my feet, and spoke: "Go home, Ezekiel. Shut yourself in the house.
3.25: Look—they gon' try to tie you up, bind you with ropes so you can't move around or speak freely.
3.26: I'm gon' shut your mouth for a time. Your tongue? It'll stick to the roof of your mouth. You won't be able to call 'em out or correct 'em—even though they rebellious.
3.27: But when I give you the cue, I'll open your mouth again. And you gon' say, 'This what the Lord God says.' Whoever wanna listen, let 'em listen. Whoever don't, that's on them. They a rebellious house, through and through."

4.1: God said, "Alright, son of man, it's time for a visual. Grab a clay tablet, lay it in front of you, and draw the city of Jerusalem on it.
4.2: Then set the scene—build up siege walls, stack up dirt mounds like you ready for war, post up army camps, and place battering rams all around. Show how the enemy gon' pull up on Jerusalem.
4.3: And take an iron plate—set it like a wall between you and the city. Lock your gaze on it. Face it like it's personal. That's the message: this city under siege, and it ain't no way out. That right there gon' be a sign for all Israel."
4.4: "Now here's where it gets heavy—lay on your left side. Symbolically take on all the mess, all the guilt, all the sin of Israel. You gon' hold it.
4.5: I'm giving you 390 days—one day for each year they been wildin'. That's how long you gon' lay there, takin' on their foolishness.
4.6: When that's done, flip to your right side. Now you hold Judah's sin—forty days. One day per year. Same deal.
4.7: The whole time, keep your face locked on that Jerusalem setup. Arm bare. Ready to prophesy against it like a one-man army.
4.8: And just so you don't get slick and flip sides early—I'ma hold you in place. You ain't movin' till the time is up."
4.9: "Now, for your food: gather wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt. Mix 'em all together in one pot and make bread out of it. That's what you gon' eat for those 390 days.
4.10: But it ain't a feast. You eat 20 shekels of it a day—rationed out. Small bites, spread thin.
4.11: Same with your water—measure it out. One-sixth of a hin. Sip slow, because that's all you got.
4.12: And this gon' shock the people: bake that bread like a barley cake, but use human waste for fuel. Yeah, let 'em see you cookin' with that. This gon' show how foul it's gon' be when they exiled."
4.13: Then God said, "This how the Israelites gon' eat—defiled food, in foreign lands, far from home. That's the consequence."
4.14: I said, "Lord God! Please! I've never defiled myself like that—not ever. I don't eat roadkill or animals torn up by beasts. I don't touch unclean food. I've kept it clean since I was a kid."
4.15: And God, full of mercy, said, "Alright. I'll let you use cow dung instead of human waste. Bake your bread over that."
4.16: Then He hit me with another word: "Son of man, I'ma cut off the food supply in Jerusalem. Folks gon' weigh out bread in fear. Gon' drink water with trembling hands.
4.17: They'll be lookin' at each other confused, sick with worry, wastin' away from their sin. They gon' know this is judgment. And it's real."

5.1: God said, "Alright, son of man, grab a sharp sword—use it like clippers. Shave your head and beard clean off. Then pull out some scales and divide up that hair. This ain't for style—this symbolic.
5.2: Burn one-third of it in the city when the siege ends. Take another third and slash it up with a sword around the city. And the last third? Toss it in the wind—I'ma send swords chasin' after it.
5.3: Now take a small handful, just a remnant, and tuck it in your clothes—right in the hem.
5.4: But then, even from that little bit, pull some out again and toss it in the fire. Burn it. Because from that fire? Flames gon' spread through all Israel."
5.5: "This what the Lord God says: This is Jerusalem. I put her right in the center of the nations—surrounded by everybody else.
5.6: But instead of leadin' right, she wilded out worse than the nations around her. Disrespected My rules. Ignored My commands. Acted like she ain't know Me at all.
5.7: So because y'all broke My laws even harder than the heathens? Didn't even try to act right? Not even on their level?
5.8: I, the Lord, am comin' against you. I'm bout to make an example outta you in front of everybody.
5.9: What I'm about to do to y'all? Never been done before. And I won't do it again. That's how deep y'all in it.
5.10: Fathers gon' eat their sons. Sons gon' eat their fathers. This ain't no metaphor. Judgment gon' hit that hard. And whoever survives? I'm scatterin' you to the wind."
5.11: "As surely as I live," says the Lord God, "because y'all defiled My sanctuary—brought in filth, idols, and nasty habits—I'ma cut you down. I ain't sparin' nobody. No mercy.
5.12: One-third of y'all gon' die from disease and starvation. One-third gon' get dropped by the sword. And the last third? Y'all gon' be scattered, but I'ma still have swords followin' you.
5.13: That's how My anger gon' cool off. My fury gon' be spent. They'll know I'm the Lord when I unleash all this in full force.
5.14: I'ma leave your city lookin' like a wasteland—an embarrassment to every nation walkin' by. Straight shame.
5.15: Folks gon' look at what happened to you and shake their heads. Gon' talk about it like a horror story. Lesson learned, example made. I said it. The Lord.
5.16: When I send famine your way—deadly arrows of destruction—they gon' hit. Bread supply? Gone. Starvin' gon' be the norm.
5.17: And on top of that? Wild animals gon' take y'all kids. Plagues and bloodshed gon' sweep through the streets. And the sword? It's still comin'. I, the Lord, have spoken."

6.1: The word of the Lord came to me again, sayin':
6.2: "Son of man, turn your face toward the mountains of Israel and start speakin' against 'em.
6.3: Tell the mountains, the hills, the valleys, the ravines—'Yo, listen up! This what the Lord God say: I'm comin' through with the sword. And I'm about to tear down every single one of y'all's high places.'
6.4: All them altars you built? Gon'. The incense spots? Crushed. And the folks who bowed down there? They bodies gon' be layin' face-down in front of them fake gods they loved so much.
6.5: I'ma throw y'all corpses down in front of them same idols. Scattered bones all around the altars. No honor. No peace.
6.6: Every place y'all lived gon' be wrecked. Cities? Gone. High places? Desolate. Altars smashed. Idols broken. Incense spots burned out. And everything y'all made with your hands? Abolished.
6.7: Dead bodies everywhere. In the middle of all this? Y'all gon' finally know I'm the Lord."
6.8: "But I ain't wiping everybody out. I'ma leave a remnant. A few of y'all gon' make it out alive, scattered in other countries, far from home.
6.9: And while y'all sittin' in them foreign lands, some of y'all gon' remember Me. Y'all gon' realize how y'all broke My heart with that adulterous spirit—chasin' every idol that caught your eye. Y'all stepped out on Me. When it hit you? Y'all gon' hate what you did. Sick of yourselves for all the nasty things y'all was doin'.
6.10: And when that happens, y'all gon' know I wasn't just talkin' to talk. I meant every word of that judgment I said was comin'."
6.11: "Now go on, son of man—pound your fists. Stomp your feet. Let the people feel the weight of this word. Say, 'Woe to all the disgusting sins Israel's out here doin'! They gon' die by sword, by famine, and by disease.'
6.12: Don't matter where they at—far off? Disease gon' catch 'em. Close by? Sword gon' slice 'em. Trapped inside the city? Starvation gon' eat 'em alive. That's how I'm lettin' My anger out."
6.13: "Then y'all gon' know I ain't playin'. Y'all gon' see the dead bodies laid out by their idols, by the altars, on every hilltop, every mountaintop, under every leafy tree, under every big ol' oak—anywhere they thought was a good place to burn sweet incense to fake gods.
6.14: I'ma stretch My hand against y'all and make the whole land desolate. Wiped clean. Worse than the wasteland by Diblah. Everywhere they used to live? Ghost town. Then they'll know—I am the Lord."

7.1: The word of the Lord came to me again:
7.2: "Son of man, speak this to Israel: 'It's the end. You hear Me? The end. It's hittin' every corner of this land.
7.3: The end is knockin' on your door now. And I ain't holdin' back no more—My anger comin' full force. I'm gon' judge you based on your actions, And pay you back for all the dirty things you done.
7.4: Don't expect mercy. Don't expect a pass. I'm givin' you exactly what you earned. Your sins gon' rise up in your own face, And then you gon' know—I'm the Lord."
7.5: "This what the Lord God say: Disaster. One big, unstoppable disaster. Look—it's already here.
7.6: The end done arrived. Time's up. Ain't no delay. It's dawning right now, and it's all comin' down.
7.7: Doom is here, y'all. This ain't no time for celebrations in the hills. This a day of trouble, not joy.
7.8: My fury comin' down on you heavy. I'm emptyin' My anger all the way out. You gon' be judged, and paid in full for your wicked ways.
7.9: Don't expect Me to flinch or feel sorry. I'm not blinkin'. I'm not lookin away. Your mess is comin' back on you—and I'm the One bringin' it. Then you gon' know who I am. I'm the One who strikes."
7.10: "Look—the day's here. Doom's already movin'. Arrogance blossomed, pride popped off, And now? Violence got a whole baton in its hand like a relay runner.
7.11: Wickedness is struttin' through the city like it run things. But ain't nobody safe. Not one person, not one crew, not one family. And don't expect tears—ain't nobody cryin' over this.
7.12: The time is now. The day is close. Don't get hype if you just bought somethin'. Don't mourn if you just sold somethin'. God's wrath comin' for everybody.
7.13: And don't think you gon' get your stuff back, even if you still alive. This vision applies to everybody. Ain't no exceptions. And if you been livin' foul, Ain't nothin' gon' give you strength now."
7.14: "They blowin' trumpets like they ready for battle, But nobody movin'. God's wrath done froze the whole squad.
7.15: Outside, the sword gon' cut folks down. Inside? Starvation and sickness gon' take the rest. Field or city—it don't matter. Death everywhere.
7.16: Whoever makes it out alive? They gon' run to the mountains, weepin' like doves, Each one cryin' over how dirty they've been.
7.17: Every hand gon' be limp. Every knee gon' feel like jelly. No strength, no courage, just fear.
7.18: Sackcloth on their bodies, Terror on their faces, Shame on every head, And bald patches where grief done snatched their pride."
7.19: "They gon' throw silver in the streets, Gold like it's trash. All that money? Can't save 'em. It won't feed their souls, won't fill their stomachs. Greed was the very trap that took 'em out.
7.20: They took the beauty I gave 'em and turned it into idols. Turned My blessings into blasphemy. So now? It's garbage to Me.
7.21: I'ma let foreigners come take all of it. Evil folks gon' raid it. And when they touch it? It's defiled.
7.22: I'm turnin' My face away. They gon' invade My sacred space, Even the most secret places. Robbers gon' stroll in and ruin everything."
7.23: "Start makin' chains. This land soaked in blood. The whole city overflowin' with violence.
7.24: So I'ma bring in the worst of the nations. They takin' over houses, And I'ma shut down the pride of the strong. Even the sacred spots gon' be desecrated.
7.25: Destruction is here. They gon' look for peace—but it won't exist.
7.26: Disaster after disaster. Rumors on top of rumors. They gon' run to prophets—nothin'. The priests? Don't have no law left. The elders? Ain't got no advice.
7.27: The king gon' mourn, The prince gon' be numb with shock, And the people? Shakin' in fear. I'm gon' judge them exactly how they lived. They reapin' what they sowed. And then—then—they gon' know: I am the Lord."

8.1: It was year six, month six, day five—I was sittin' in the crib, chillin' with some of the elders of Judah, when boom—the hand of the Lord God came down on me heavy.
8.2: I looked up and saw what looked like a man made of fire—waist down, full flame; waist up, glowing like amber, shinin' like glory.
8.3: Then He reached out—looked like a hand—and grabbed me by a lock of my hair. The Spirit lifted me between heaven and earth and dropped me off in a vision, right in Jerusalem, at the entrance of the inner court's north gate—where that scandalous "idol of jealousy" was sittin', makin' God mad on sight.
8.4: But even with all that, the glory of the God of Israel was still there—just like I saw back in the plains.
8.5: He said, "Son of man, look up toward the north." So I looked—and boom, there it was. That same idol of jealousy sittin' at the entrance, bold and disrespectful.
8.6: He said, "You see this mess? This what Israel out here doin' in My own house—things so foul they drivin' Me away from My own sanctuary. But hold up—keep watchin'. It gets worse."
8.7: He took me to the outer court. I saw a hole in the wall.
8.8: He said, "Dig in." So I dug through the wall—there was a door behind it.
8.9: He said, "Go in and look at the filth they tryna hide."
8.10: I stepped in and saw it—walls covered with every creepy, filthy creature you could think of. Nasty animals and idol drawings everywhere—this was Israel's hidden idol gallery.
8.11: And standing right there? Seventy elders of Israel. All up in it. Burning incense. One of 'em—Jaazaniah, son of Shaphan—was leadin' the whole vibe. Cloud of smoke rising like it was holy, but it was pure abomination.
8.12: God said, "You see this? These so-called leaders think I don't see them. They actin' like I done left the land, so now they worshipin' in the dark—each one got his own private idol room. Secret sins on display."
8.13: Then He said, "Come on, it gets worse."
8.14: He brought me to the north gate of the Lord's house again—and what I see? Women sittin' there cryin' for Tammuz, some false god from the streets. Heartbreakin', but not for Me—for that idol.
8.15: He said, "You see this? You ain't seen nothin' yet."
8.16: Then He took me inside the inner court—right by the temple porch. And there were about twenty-five men. But get this—they had their backs to the temple of the Lord and they was facin' east, bowin' down to the sun. Turned their back on God, literally.
8.17: He said, "You see this, son of man? You think this some light offense? These folks out here doin' the most—disrespectin' Me in My own house, floodin' the land with violence, and still tryna provoke Me. They even got the nerve to do this little 'branch to the nose' gesture—like they makin' fun of Me!"
8.18: "So I'ma act. And I ain't holdin' back. I ain't sparin' nobody, and I ain't listenin' to no fake tears. They could scream loud as they want—I'm not hearin' 'em."

9.1: Then I heard Him call out with a booming voice: "Bring the enforcers. The ones responsible for this city—each one need to show up strapped, weapon in hand."
9.2: And just like that, six men came walkin' from the upper gate that faces north. Every one of them had a battle-ax in hand, ready for business. But one of 'em stood out—dressed in linen, lookin' clean. He had a scribe's kit on his hip, like he was takin' names. They all rolled up and posted by the bronze altar.
9.3: Then the glory of the God of Israel lifted up from between the cherubim and moved to the entrance of the temple. And God spoke to the man in linen with the writing gear:
9.4: "Go through the city—walk through Jerusalem—and mark the foreheads of everyone who mourns and cries over the nasty, evil stuff goin' on. The ones still grievin' over sin? Mark 'em."
9.5: Then He turned to the other six and said, "Now y'all follow right behind him. And when you do—wipe everybody else out. Don't hesitate. Don't show pity.
9.6: Old men, young men, women, kids—all of 'em. If they don't got that mark, take 'em out. But don't you dare touch anyone with the mark. Start at My house. Start at the sanctuary." So they began right there—with the elders, the so-called leaders, who were in front of the temple.
9.7: God said, "Y'all see what they turned My house into? Fill these courts with the bodies. Let this place feel the weight of what's been done. Now go out and finish it in the city." And they did.
9.8: While all this was happening, I was left there, shook and alone. I fell on my face and cried out, "Lord God… is You really about to wipe out everybody that's left? Even the few that's still here in Jerusalem? Is this it?"
9.9: He said, "Listen, Ezekiel. The sin in Israel and Judah? It's off the charts. The land is soaked in blood. The city is full of twisted, violent acts. And the people? They bold with it. They say, 'God don't see us. He gone. Ain't nobody watchin.'"
9.10: But Me? I ain't sparin' nobody. I'm not lookin' away. I'm givin' everybody exactly what they deserve."
9.11: Then, right on time, the man in linen—the one with the inkhorn—came back and said, "It's done. I did everything You told me to."

10.1: I looked up—and there it was again. Above the heads of the cherubim, in that glowing space, sat something like a throne. Looked like deep sapphire, royal and radiant.
10.2: Then God spoke to the man in linen: "Go in between the wheels, under the cherubim. Scoop up them hot coals from between 'em and scatter the fire all over the city." And he did—walked in right as I watched.
10.3: The cherubim were standin' on the south side of the temple when the linen-clothed man stepped in, and suddenly, whoosh!—a thick cloud filled the inner court.
10.4: The glory of the Lord rose up from the cherubim's position and paused right at the temple door. The whole place got hazy—thick with smoke and light. That glory hit different. Even the outer court was lit up with the presence of the Lord.
10.5: And the sound? The wings of them cherubim flappin' echoed through the courts—loud like the voice of the Almighty Himself.
10.6: Then it happened. God gave the command again: "Grab fire from the wheels between the cherubim." The man in linen stepped up next to the wheels.
10.7: One of the cherubim reached into the fire, pulled out a burning coal, and dropped it in the linen man's hands. He took it and dipped.
10.8: And under their wings, the cherubim had hands—human-looking hands, hidden beneath the glory.
10.9: Then I looked at the wheels—four of 'em, one for each cherub. Shimmering like beryl stone. But again—this wasn't your average wheel setup.
10.10: All four looked exactly the same: like a wheel inside another wheel—interlocking, multidimensional, supernatural.
10.11: When they moved, they didn't turn or curve—they went straight ahead in whichever direction the cherub's face was pointing.
10.12: Their whole bodies—backs, hands, wings, even the wheels—covered in eyes. They was seein' everything. Every angle. Nothing missed.
10.13: And I heard the name for them: "Wheel."
10.14: Each cherub had four faces: A cherub face, A human face, A lion's face, And an eagle's face.
10.15: The cherubim lifted off the ground—same heavenly beings I saw by the River Chebar. Ain't no doubt.
10.16: When they moved, the wheels moved too. When they rose up, the wheels rose right with 'em. They stayed in sync—one spirit in all of them.
10.17: When the cherubim paused, the wheels paused. When they lifted, the wheels lifted too. They was linked deep, spiritually.
10.18: Then the glory of the Lord moved again. It lifted from the temple entrance and hovered above the cherubim.
10.19: And the cherubim spread their wings and rose from the earth—right in front of me. The wheels rolled right with them. They stopped at the east gate of the Lord's house. And there, above them, rested the glory of the God of Israel.
10.20: I recognized them. These were the same beings I saw in that wild vision by the Chebar River. No doubt—they were cherubim.
10.21: Each had four faces. Each had four wings. And under the wings? Human hands again.
10.22: The faces looked exactly like the ones I saw by the river. No changes. Same presence. Same glory. And just like before—they moved straight ahead. No turning, no hesitation. Just holy purpose.

11.1: Then the Spirit picked me up again and took me to the East Gate of the Lord's house—the one that faces east. And there, standin' at the gate, was twenty-five men. Two names stood out: Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah—these dudes had status, princes of the people.
11.2: God said, "Son of man, see them? These the ones cookin' up evil schemes and givin' foul advice in this city.
11.3: They walkin' around sayin', 'It ain't time to build nothin'. This city's the pot, and we the good meat.' They think they safe in the stew—untouchable in the middle."
11.4: God said, "Prophesy against 'em, son. Go ahead, speak My Word."
11.5: Then the Spirit of the Lord dropped on me heavy and said, "Speak up, Ezekiel! This what the Lord says: Y'all been talkin' slick, but I know exactly what's in y'all heads.
11.6: Y'all done stacked bodies in these streets. The blood of the innocent cryin' out from every corner.
11.7: So here's what I say: Those bodies? They the meat. This city? Yeah, it's the pot. But you—you the ones gettin' pulled out and judged.
11.8: You scared of the sword? Cool. 'Cause that's exactly what's comin' for you.
11.9: I'ma pull you out this city and hand you over to strangers. Judgment gon' hit you hard.
11.10: You gon' die by the sword—outside the city, at the border of Israel. Then you'll finally realize I am the Lord.
11.11: Nah, this city ain't gon' protect you like no caldron. You ain't the prize meat. You gon' be judged at the border, and it'll be too late.
11.12: Why? 'Cause you ain't walked in My ways. You ain't kept My standards. You out here actin' like the world around you. So now you gon' feel what that lifestyle brings."
11.13: While I was speakin' this word, Pelatiah—yep, the leader—dropped dead on the spot. I fell on my face, cryin' loud: "Lord God! You gon' wipe out everybody that's left? Ain't gon' be no remnant?"
11.14: Then the Word of the Lord came again:
11.15: "Son of man, your people—the ones in exile, the outcasts, the ones the folks in Jerusalem wrote off—they say, 'Y'all far from the Lord now. This land belong to us.'
11.16: But tell 'em this: Even though I scattered y'all, Even though y'all in foreign lands, I've been a sanctuary to you out there—a holy place in the middle of captivity.
11.17: And now I'm sayin': I'ma bring y'all back. I'ma gather you from the nations, bring you home to the land of Israel.
11.18: And when y'all get back? You gon' clean house. Tear down the idols. Get rid of all that nasty, fake worship.
11.19: Then I'ma do a heart transplant. Give you one heart. Put a new spirit in you. Take out that cold, stone heart… and give you a soft heart that can actually feel Me again.
11.20: You gon' walk in My ways, live by My laws, and keep it real. You'll be My people. And I'll be your God.
11.21: But for the ones still chasin' idols and filth? They gon' get what's comin' to them. I ain't forget." That's what the Lord God said.
11.22: Then the cherubim lifted their wings again—wheels rollin' with 'em—and the glory of the God of Israel was hoverin' right above.
11.23: God's glory rose up from the city… and stood over the mountain to the east. God left the temple.
11.24: The Spirit lifted me and brought me back to Babylon, to the exiles—just like that. The vision ended, and I was back in real time.
11.25: Then I opened my mouth and told the exiles everything God showed me.

12.1: The word of the Lord came to me, again:
12.2: "Son of man, you livin' right in the middle of a rebellious house. They got eyes, but won't see. They got ears, but don't hear. Hardheaded. Blind on purpose.
12.3: So here's what you gon' do—pack up your stuff like somebody gettin' taken into exile. Do it in broad daylight, so everybody see you movin'. Go from your spot to another place. Maybe, just maybe, they'll get the message.
12.4: Drag your stuff out during the day so they see it. Then at night, go out again—like someone bein' forced out they home.
12.5: Dig through the wall while they watch. Crawl out through the hole with your baggage. Make a scene—they need to feel this.
12.6: Carry your bag on your shoulder as the sun goin' down. Cover your face—like you don't even wanna look at the land no more. This whole act? It's a sign. A message for the people of Israel."
12.7: So I did what He said. In the daylight, I packed my things like an exile. That night, I dug through the wall with my hands, carried my stuff out on my shoulder at twilight—all in front of them.
12.8: The next morning, God spoke again:
12.9: "Son of man, I know they askin' you, 'What you doin'? What's all this?'
12.10: Tell them: This here? It's a word from the Lord. It's about the prince in Jerusalem and everybody else still in the city.
12.11: Tell 'em: 'I'm a living sign. What I just did? It's what's gon' happen to them—they headed into captivity.'
12.12: And that prince? He gon' carry his stuff on his shoulder too, sneak out at night. He gon' dig through the wall and try to escape with his face covered—ashamed, scared, tryin' not to look down.
12.13: But I'ma catch him. My net gon' trap him. I'll take him to Babylon, but he won't see it—though he gon' die there.
12.14: All his boys, all his soldiers? I'm scatterin' 'em like dust. And I'm still comin' with the sword right behind 'em.
12.15: Then they'll know who I am—when I scatter 'em across the nations and drop 'em off in foreign lands.
12.16: But I'll let a few survive. Just a remnant—spared from famine, disease, and violence. And they gon' talk about what they did, gon' confess it in front of the nations. Then they'll know I am the Lord."
12.18: "Son of man, now eat your food like you're scared—hands shakin', breath unsteady. Drink your water like you nervous and stressed out.
12.19: Tell the people: This is what the Lord says to Jerusalem and Israel—'Y'all gon' eat bread with anxiety and drink water in fear. Why? Because the land's about to be emptied out. The violence of the people done cursed the place.'
12.20: The cities? Gon'. The land? Desolate. And y'all gon' know who I am when it's done."
12.22: "Son of man, they got a saying in Israel: 'These visions take forever. Nothing ever really happens.'
12.23: Tell them: 'God said—that little saying is done. Y'all ain't gon' use it no more.' Instead, say: 'The time is now. Every word and every vision is comin' to pass.'
12.24: Ain't gon' be no more false visions. No more hype prophets sellin' sweet lies.
12.25: I'm the Lord. When I speak, it happens. No more delays. This generation gon' see it with their own eyes."
12.27: "Son of man, they still tryna play it off, sayin', 'These prophecies ain't for us. That's way in the future.'
12.28: Tell them: 'God said—ain't nothin' I said gon' be postponed. It's gon' happen now. I said it, and I'ma do it.'"

13.1: The word of the Lord came to me again:
13.2: "Son of man, I need you to prophesy against the prophets of Israel—the ones runnin' their mouths like they speakin' for Me but really just speakin' from their own little hearts. Tell 'em: 'This the Word of the Lord.'
13.3: The Lord God says: Woe to these foolish prophets—chasin' their own feelings like it's the Spirit... talkin' like they seen somethin' when they ain't seen a thing!
13.4: Y'all prophets are like foxes in the desert—slick, sneaky, and ain't helpin' nobody.
13.5: Y'all didn't step into the broken places. You ain't built no walls to protect My people. You ain't preppin' them for battle on the Day of the Lord.
13.6: Instead, you out here talkin' loud with empty visions. Lyin' in My name like, 'The Lord says...' But I never sent you. Y'all out here hopin' your lie gon' come true.
13.7: But let's be real—y'all ain't seen nothin'. Y'all makin' it up. You keep throwin' My name on your own imagination. I didn't say a word."
13.8: "So because of that—because y'all spittin' nonsense and droppin' false visions—I'm comin' for you," says the Lord.
13.9: "My hand is against y'all fake prophets who out here makin' up lies. You won't be part of My people. Your names ain't goin' in the roll book. You ain't settin' foot in My land. And then? You'll know I'm the Lord God."
13.10: "Y'all been slick with it. Tellin' My people, 'Peace is comin'!' when peace ain't even on the menu. You build weak walls—phony foundations—and then cover it with cheap plaster, like that's gon' hold.
13.11: So go tell the ones plasterin' over these lies: That wall gon' fall. Storms comin', heavy rain, hail, winds that'll tear the whole thing down.
13.12: And when it crumbles? They gon' ask, 'Where's that plaster you was braggin' about?'"
13.13: "I'm sendin' a storm full of fury. Rain, hail, wind—My anger unleashed.
13.14: That wall y'all covered with spiritual nonsense? I'm breakin' it down to the foundation. And when it falls, y'all fall with it. Then you'll know—I'm the Lord.
13.15: I'll make it known—I'm settin' fire to the wall and the ones who lied to build it.
13.16: Y'all prophets that keep talkin' about peace in Jerusalem when I never said that? Yeah—they gone too."
13.17: "Son of man, now turn toward the daughters of your people—the ones out here usin' fake spiritualism, pretendin' to prophesy.
13.18: Tell 'em: 'Woe to y'all women who out here sewing up little charms, tyin' spells on people, throwin' veils over folks like you got mystical powers—hunting souls like prey. Y'all savin' your own necks while trappin' innocent folks.'
13.19: You sell Me out over a slice of bread and a handful of grain. Killin' off folks that should've lived, and protectin' folks that should've been judged—All with lies. Lies My people actually believe."
13.20: "So I'm sayin this: I'm comin' for your little charms—the ones you use to trap souls like birds. I'ma rip them off and let My people go free.
13.21: I'ma tear off them veils, too. You ain't gon' have My people in your grip no more. They ain't gon' be your victims. And then you'll know I'm the Lord."
13.22: "You out here hurtin' the righteous with your lies—they heart broken and confused, and I didn't send that pain. Meanwhile, you hypin' up the wicked, givin' them false comfort so they don't turn around and get saved.
13.23: So now it's over. No more fake visions. No more hoodoo divinations. I'ma snatch My people out y'all hands. And when I do? You gon' know—I am the Lord."

14.1: Some of the elders of Israel came and sat down in front of me like they wanted a word.
14.2: Then the Lord spoke to me, real direct:
14.3: "Son of man, these men got idols—not on a shelf, but in their hearts. They done set up things that make 'em stumble into sin. And now they wanna ask Me for a word? You think I'ma let 'em treat Me like some fortune teller when their hearts already full of betrayal?"
14.4: "Go tell 'em this: 'This what the Lord says: If anybody from Israel got idols buried in their heart and still tryna come inquire of Me? I'ma answer them alright—but through the weight of those very idols they clingin' to.
14.5: I'm about to grab the heart of Israel—because they done ran far from Me, caught up in false gods and side pieces."
14.6: "So go ahead and tell the house of Israel: Repent. Turn from them idols. Turn your face away from all the mess you've been entertainin'.
14.7: 'Cause if anybody—Israelite or foreigner—pulls away from Me and sets up idols in their heart, then tries to come to the prophet lookin' for a word from the Lord? Nah. I ain't usin' the prophet. I'ma deal with him Myself.
14.8: I'ma set My face against him. Make him a cautionary tale, a walking proverb. Cut him off from My people—then they'll know who I am."
14.9: "And if the prophet gets swayed and speaks something? I allowed it—to expose him. But don't get it twisted—I'ma stretch My hand against that prophet too.
14.10: Both of 'em—the one askin' and the one prophesyin'—gon' be held accountable. Same judgment, same guilt.
14.11: So maybe then My people will stop strayin', stop trashin' My name, and finally walk right—so I can be their God, and they can be Mine."
14.12: Then the word of the Lord came to me again:
14.13: "Son of man, when a land straight-up betrays Me—over and over—I step in. I'll shut down their food supply, send famine, and remove life—man and beast alike.
14.14: And let Me be clear: even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were livin' there, they could only save themselves. Their righteousness ain't stretchin' to nobody else."
14.15: "If I let wild animals roam the streets and run folks off the land, even then—Noah, Daniel, and Job could only save themselves. No sons. No daughters.
14.16: They'd walk out, but the land? Still desolate.
14.17: If I send a sword through the land, sayin', 'Go ahead, cut down everything'—same thing. Only them three righteous men would make it out.
14.18: No kids. No crew. Just them.
14.19: Or if I let disease hit like a plague—people droppin', judgment fallin'—Noah, Daniel, and Job? Still wouldn't save nobody but themselves.
14.20: I mean it. They'd survive 'cause of their walk—but not even their own family would be spared."
14.21: "So what y'all think gon' happen when I drop all four judgments on Jerusalem? Sword, famine, wild beasts, and disease—all at once? Ain't nothin' gon' be left. Man or animal.
14.22: But... I'll still leave a remnant. A few sons and daughters gon' make it out. And when they show up to you, when you see how they live and what they've been through, you'll understand.
14.23: They'll help you realize that I ain't just wildin' out. Everything I did—I had a reason. You'll see it with your own eyes."

15.1: Then the word of the Lord came to me:
15.2: "Son of man, let Me ask you this—What makes vine wood so special? What makes it better than any other tree in the forest?
15.3: Can you use vine wood to build somethin'? Can you even make a peg outta it to hang a pot on?
15.4: Nah. It's soft, twisted, fragile. So what happens? It gets tossed in the fire for fuel. It burns from both ends, and the middle gets scorched too. Tell Me—what's left that's useful?
15.5: Even when it was whole, you couldn't make nothin' out of it. So how much more useless is it once it's been through the fire?
15.6: "This is what the Lord God says: Just like that useless vine wood you throw in the fire, that's how I'm handin' over the people of Jerusalem.
15.7: I've turned My face against them. They might escape one fire, but they gon' land in another. And when that happens, they'll know—I am the Lord.
15.8: I'm makin' the land desolate. Why? 'Cause they won't stop bein' unfaithful. They just keep breakin' the covenant, keep pushin Me away. That's what the Lord God said."

16.1: The word of the Lord hit me again:
16.2: "Son of man, let Jerusalem know just how filthy her sins really are.
16.3: Say this to her: 'This what the Lord God says to Jerusalem: You was born in Canaan land—your daddy was an Amorite and your mama was a Hittite.
16.4: When you came out the womb, nobody even cared. Your umbilical cord wasn't cut. You weren't washed off. Nobody rubbed you with salt or wrapped you up warm. You were just—
16.5: Tossed out like trash in an open field, left to die. No one pitied you. Nobody had compassion. They looked at you and said, 'Ew, throw that away.'
16.6: But I came by and saw you, baby girl, squirming in your own blood. And I said, 'Live.' Yeah, even in your mess, I told you twice: LIVE.
16.7: Then I raised you up like a wildflower in the field. You grew tall and strong. Your body matured, your hair came in—But you was still naked and bare.
16.8: I came back again and saw you. This time, you were grown—it was time for love. So I spread My robe over you and covered your shame. I made a covenant with you. I claimed you as Mine, says the Lord God.
16.9: I washed you clean. Got all the blood off you. Anointed you with oil.
16.10: I dressed you in embroidered clothes, gave you shoes made from the best leather. Wrapped you in fine linen and silk.
16.11: I hooked you up with bracelets, a chain for your neck,
16.12: a jewel in your nose, earrings for your ears, and a beautiful crown for your head.
16.13: Girl, you were dripping—gold, silver, fine linen, silk, embroidered threads. You ate the best—flour, honey, and oil. You were gorgeous, royalty even.
16.14: Word got out. Nations were talking about you. You were flawless—because of MY glory that I placed on you," says the Lord God.
16.15: "But you? You started feelin' yourself. You trusted your own beauty. Turned your fame into a hustle—you started hoein'.
16.16: You took the clothes I gave you and built shrines on the high places—then laid down with whoever walked by. Disgusting.
16.17: You used the gold and silver I gave you, melted it down into male images—then did nasty things with 'em.
16.18: You burned incense to those fake gods using MY oil. Wrapped them in MY garments.
16.19: You set MY food in front of them like it was a peace offering. The same food I fed you. The same honey, oil, flour. And yep, that's how it went down," says the Lord God.
16.20: "Worse than that—you took MY kids, the sons and daughters you birthed for ME, and burned them alive as sacrifices.
16.21: You killed My babies, passed them through the fire. And for what? For them?
16.22: And after all that filth, you never stopped to remember when I found you—naked, bleeding, helpless in your own blood.
16.23: "Then—after all that mess—Woe, woe to you!" says the Lord God.
16.24: You built shrines on every corner.
16.25: Set up shop at the top of every street. You made yourself cheap. You let anyone in. You turned your beauty into shame.
16.26: You gave yourself to Egypt too—your neighbors with the strong bodies. But you ain't stop there. You was out here doing the most.
16.27: So I stepped in. I pulled back My blessings. Let the Philistines—who don't even know Me—see your wild ways and get disgusted.
16.28: Then you turned to Assyria. You was never satisfied. Still out here giving yourself away.
16.29: You even reached all the way out to Chaldea—land of traders. But even they couldn't fill that empty space.
16.30: How sick is your heart?" says the Lord God. "You act like a bold-faced harlot—no shame, no brakes."
16.31: "You ain't even like the other sex workers—at least they got paid. You gave it up for free—built shrines, set up shop on every street.
16.32: You straight-up cheated like a wife who don't want her man. You welcomed strangers instead of staying loyal.
16.33: Most prostitutes get paid. But YOU paid your lovers. You hired men to sleep with you.
16.34: You flipped the whole game. Ain't nobody chasing you—you chasing them. You paying them. You ain't getting nothing back."
16.36: This is what the Lord God says: Because you threw yourself around, stripped yourself in public, and shed the blood of My children—because of all your nasty idols—
16.37: I'ma gather all your lovers—old flames and new ones, the ones you loved and even the ones you hated—bring 'em all together, and expose your nakedness in front of them.
16.38: I'ma judge you like I do women who cheat or murder—judgment gon' hit you with blood, fury, and jealousy.
16.39: I'ma hand you over. They gon' tear down your shrines, break your idols, snatch your jewels, rip your clothes—leave you naked and bare.
16.40: They gon' form a mob, stone you, and slice you down with swords.
16.41: They gon' burn your house down, make a public example out of you. Your lil' side hustle of harlotry? It's over. No more lovers, no more payin' for attention.
16.42: Then, and only then, will My anger be satisfied. My jealousy gon' cool down. I'll be done.
16.43: But know this: Because you forgot your beginnings, and made Me mad with all your drama, I'ma pay you back. You gon' feel every bit of what you did," says the Lord God.
16.44: "Everybody gon' say this about you: 'Like mother, like daughter.'
16.45: You just like your mama—didn't love your man, didn't love your kids. Your sisters just as wild. Your people? Amorites and Hittites.
16.46: Big sister Samaria lives up north. Little sister Sodom down south.
16.47: You ain't just walk in their mess—you ran past them. You outdid 'em in wickedness.
16.48: As I live," says the Lord God, "Sodom ain't even do what you and your girls have done.
16.49: Sodom's sin was pride, greed, and laziness. They didn't help the poor or needy.
16.50: They were arrogant and did foul things in My face. So I wiped 'em out.
16.51: Samaria only did HALF of what you've done. You made them look righteous by comparison.
16.52: So since you love to judge your sisters—carry your own shame now. You worse than both of them."
16.53: "One day I'ma restore their fortunes—Sodom, Samaria, and even yours, Jerusalem.
16.54: And when that day comes, you gon' be ashamed. 'Cause the very ones you looked down on? I'ma bring them back up next to you.
16.55: They gon' rise again. And so will you and your daughters—but not 'cause of anything you did.
16.56: Back when you were on top, Sodom was a joke to you. But now? Look at you.
16.57: The people you used to shame—the Syrians, the Philistines—they mockin' you now.
16.58: You reaping what you sowed," says the Lord.
16.59: "You broke the covenant. So now I'ma deal with you."
16.60: "But still... I remember the promise I made to you when you were young. And I'ma make a new covenant—an everlasting one.
16.61: You gon' remember everything you did and hang your head low. And when I bring your sisters back into the fold, you'll see they've become daughters to you—not by your covenant, but by Mine.
16.62: I'ma re-establish the covenant. And you gon' know—I am the Lord.
16.63: You gon' be so ashamed, you won't even be able to speak. But I'll cover it all. I'll make atonement for everything you did," says the Lord God.

17.1: Then God hit Ezekiel with another Word.
17.2: "Son of man, I need you to drop a riddle on Israel—a parable, somethin' with layers. Tell the people:
17.3: 'This what the Lord God says: There was this big ol' eagle—wings wide, feathers long, colors poppin'. He flew over to Lebanon, pulled the top branch off a tall cedar.
17.4: He clipped the newest little twig from the top, took it to a land full of hustle and trade, and planted it in the middle of the merchant city.
17.5: But that ain't all—he grabbed some seed from the land, planted it in rich soil, close to water, like he was setting up a willow tree to flourish.
17.6: That seed turned into a vine—low to the ground, real spread out. It grew, but it stayed facing the eagle, like it knew who gave it life. Branches came out. Shoots popped up.
17.7: But then, another eagle rolled up—big wings, feathers everywhere. And guess what? That vine? It bent toward this new eagle. Stretched out its branches like, 'Come water me too!' Even though it was already planted in good soil, plenty of water, ready to bear fruit and grow strong.
17.8: The setup was perfect—this vine had everything. It was supposed to thrive. But…"
17.9: "Say to them: This is what the Lord God says: 'You think that vine gon' make it? Thrive? Really?
17.10: Nope. The first eagle gon' yank it up by the roots. Chop off the fruit. Leaves gon' wither. And it ain't even gon' take much—no army needed.
17.11: It was planted, sure. But it ain't gon' survive. As soon as that dry east wind blows? It's a wrap. Withered. Gone. In the same spot it was planted.'"
17.12: Then the Lord said, "Ezekiel, tell these hard-headed people what this really means:
17.13: That first eagle? That's the king of Babylon. He came to Jerusalem, snatched the king and his top men, and dragged them back to Babylon.
17.14: He made a deal with one of the royal kids— put him under oath, made him promise to stay loyal. He even stripped the land of the strong ones, just to keep that kingdom humble and dependent.
17.15: The plan was: stay in line, follow the covenant, and the kingdom could survive.
17.16: But what happened? That dude broke the covenant. Sent folks to Egypt tryna get horses and backup.
17.18: You think that gon' work? You think you can break a promise and still win? Nah.
17.19: As surely as I live," says the Lord God, "He gon' die in Babylon—the same place of the king he betrayed.
17.20: And don't expect Pharaoh to save him. His army won't mean a thing when Babylon builds up siege walls and cuts off everything.
17.21: He broke his word. Signed the deal and still acted shady. So now? He ain't getting away."
17.22: "This is what the Lord God says: 'Since he played Me, since he broke the covenant he made under My name, I'm gon' pay him back.
17.23: I'ma catch him in My net. He gon' be trapped, tried, and judged in Babylon for the mess he made—against Me.
17.24: His people? His crew? His soldiers? They either gon' get cut down by the sword or scattered in every direction.
17.25: And THEN they'll know—I'm the Lord. I said it. I meant it."
17.26: "But don't get it twisted," says the Lord God. "I'ma take another branch from that same cedar— the highest part, the top twig— and I'ma plant it on a high mountain in Israel.
17.27: That little twig gon' grow. It'll become a majestic cedar. Birds from everywhere gon' come nest in its shade.
17.28: And when it happens, all the trees in the field gon' realize this:
17.29: I'm the One who humbles the tall trees and lifts up the low ones. I dry up green trees and make the dry ones flourish.
17.30: I, the Lord, spoke it. And best believe—I did it."

18.1: The Lord came to Ezekiel again with a word.
18.2: "Yo, what's up with y'all repeating this line in Israel: 'The fathers ate sour grapes, and now the kids got that bitter taste?' Like they the ones sufferin' for what Daddy did?
18.3: Nah, that's dead," says the Lord God. "Y'all ain't gon' say that no more in My house.
18.4: Listen close—every soul belongs to Me. Daddy's soul, son's soul, grandbaby's soul—they all Mine. And the soul that sins? That's the one that's gon' die.
18.5: Let's say a man out here doin' right. He walkin' in truth, showin' justice.
18.6: He don't be out on them idol hills, don't bow to false gods, don't sleep with his neighbor's wife, and don't cross lines with a woman on her cycle.
18.7: He don't take from nobody, he gives back what he borrowed, don't strong-arm folks, feeds the hungry, and keeps the poor warm.
18.8: He don't charge no interest, don't scam folks, but settles beefs fair and square. He follows My laws and lives right.
18.9: That man? He good. He gon' live. I said it. Period.
18.10: Now let's say this righteous man got a son who wildin' out— stealin', killin', doin' dirt.
18.11: He out here messin' with idols, sleepin' with other men's wives,
18.12: oppressing the poor, robbing folks, keepin' what ain't his, prayin' to false gods, livin' foul.
18.13: He out here chargin' folks interest on loans, stackin' off the weak. He think he gon' live? Nah. He gon' die. His blood on him. Don't look at daddy—he made his own mess.

20.5: "Tell 'em: This what God says—'The day I picked y'all, the day I showed up in Egypt and made y'all a promise, I said, "I'm the Lord your God."

20.7: I told y'all, "Toss out all them nasty idols, stop defiling yourselves with Egyptian mess. I'm the Lord."
20.8: But y'all didn't listen. Kept your idols. Kept wildin'. So I almost snapped and wrecked y'all in Egypt.

20.14: But again, I held back—for My name's sake, so I ain't look shady to the other nations.
20.15: I even swore: 'Y'all not entering the promised land.' Why? 'Cause you chose idols over Me.
20.16: Why? 'Cause they ain't care about My laws, didn't walk right, and kept disrespectin' the Sabbath. Their hearts stayed stuck on idols.
20.17: Still, I didn't finish y'all. Mercy held Me back.
20.18: "Then I talked to your kids: 'Don't follow your parents' mess. Don't be like them.

20.22: I could've lit it all up—but for My name's sake, I showed restraint.
20.23: I told 'em: 'You gonna get scattered to the nations.'
20.24: Why? 'Cause y'all threw My laws in the trash and went back to your idols.
20.25: "So I let y'all follow bogus rules—rules that couldn't even save you.

20.27: "Tell Israel: Y'all stayed unfaithful, even after I brought you into the land I promised.
20.28: You saw them hills and trees? Ran straight up there to do idol worship like you ain't learned nothin'.
20.29: I asked, 'What is this Bamah spot y'all keep runnin' to?' And the name stuck."
20.30: "So tell 'em this: Are y'all really still doing your ancestors' nasty mess? Burning your kids in fire?

20.33: "As surely as I live," says the Lord, "I'ma rule over y'all with a strong hand—even if I gotta come in hot.

20.36: I'm putting y'all through it again—testing hearts.
20.37: I'll check you like sheep, count you, and bring you back into covenant with Me.
20.38: But the rebels? The ones still wildin'? They not coming back to the land. They'll know I'm the Lord real quick."
20.39: "House of Israel, go ahead—keep playin' with your idols if that's what you want. But don't bring that fake worship around Me. Stop disrespecting My name."
20.40: "One day, up on My holy mountain, the whole house of Israel will finally serve Me right.
20.41: I'll accept your offerings. I'll accept y'all again. I'll bring you home and the world will see y'all belong to Me.
20.42: Then you'll know I'm the Lord—when I deliver on My promise and bring y'all back to the land.
20.43: And you gon' remember everything you did—and be ashamed of how far you fell.

20.46: "Turn toward the south. Prophesy against it. Tell the forest this:
20.47: 'God said: I'm about to set a fire. Green trees, dead trees—every last one gon' burn.
20.48: The whole world will know I lit it, and no one can put it out.' "

21.1: The word of the Lord came to Ezekiel,
21.2: "Son of man, turn and face Jerusalem. Speak out against the Temple. Prophesy against all Israel.
21.3: Tell them, 'This is what God says: I'm comin' for you. I'm drawin' My sword and I ain't sparing nobody—righteous or wicked.

21.9: "Say this: A sword, a sword—sharpened and polished.

21.12: "Cry out loud, Ezekiel. Wail. It's comin' for My people—princes included. They about to feel terror. Strike your thigh, 'cause what's comin' gon' hurt."
21.13: "This sword is a test. And even the royal scepter can't stand against it. Ain't nobody exempt."
21.14: "Clap your hands, Ezekiel! Call for triple destruction. This sword gon' hit twice as hard, and it's targetin' the powerful, even in their private chambers.
21.15: I've posted it at every city gate. It's gonna break hearts and trip folks up. It shines for slaughter.
21.16: Right hand, left hand—cut wherever it gotta cut.

21.18: Then God gave Ezekiel more direction:

22.26: The priests? Don't even care what's holy or what ain't. Don't teach nobody right from wrong. Don't even honor the Sabbath. And because of that? I get disrespected daily.
22.27: The princes? Wolves. Huntin' people down just to get rich.
22.28: And the prophets? Still lyin'. Tellin' fake visions, makin' up what they think I said. I ain't say none of that!
22.29: And the people? Oppressin' folks, robbin' each other, abusin' the poor and the immigrant. Coldhearted.
22.30: I looked for just one person—one righteous soul who would stand in the gap for the land. Just one who'd build a wall and pray. But I couldn't find nobody.

23.16: As soon as she saw them, she went wild for them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.
23.17: The Babylonians came to her, to her bed of love, and defiled her with their lust. After they defiled her, she turned away from them in disgust.

23.30: These things will happen to you because you played the ho with the nations and defiled yourself with their idols.

23.39: On the same day they slaughtered their children for their idols, they entered my sanctuary and profaned it. That's what they did in my house.
23.40: They even sent for men who came from far away, and when they arrived, you bathed yourself for them, painted your eyes, and put on your jewelry.
23.41: You sat on an elegant couch, with a table set before it on which you had placed my incense and my oil.
23.42: The noise of a carefree crowd was around her; drunkards were brought in from the desert along with common men, who put bracelets on their wrists and beautiful crowns on their heads.

24.1: On the tenth day of the tenth month, ninth year of exile, God came to Ezekiel like,
24.2: "Son of man, mark this date. It's official—Babylon just laid siege to Jerusalem today. Write that down.
24.3: Now go tell that hardheaded house a lil parable: 'God said— Put a pot on the stove. Fill it up with water.
24.4: Throw in some prime cuts—thigh, shoulder, all the good meat.
24.5: Pick the best from the flock. Stack the bones like firewood. Get that thing boilin'. Let it simmer.'
24.6: But here's what God really sayin': 'Woe to that bloody city—Jerusalem. It's like a dirty pot full of scum. No matter how much you stir it, the mess won't go away.
24.7: Blood's been spilled right in the open, not even hidden. Ain't nobody tryin' to bury the bodies.
24.8: I let it stay on the surface to stir up My fury—no covering, no excuses.'"
24.9: "So now I'm sayin again," God says: 'Woe to that bloody city! I'ma build this fire high.
24.10: Stack the wood. Let it blaze. Cook everything down till it's burnt. Let the bones turn black.
24.11: Then set that empty pot on the coals till the bronze glows red— til the filth melts off and that nasty scum's gone.
24.12: Y'all been wearin Me out with all these lies, still holdin' on to your dirt. Let that fire purify what y'all won't let go of.'
24.13: 'Your filth is deep-rooted. I tried to cleanse you—but you refused. So I ain't tryna wash you no more. I'ma let My fury run its course.
24.14: I said what I said, and I ain't takin' it back. You gon' get judged by your own actions and your own deeds. That's on Me. I'm the Lord.'"
24.15: Then God came to Ezekiel with a hard word:
24.16: "Son of man, I'm takin' your wife—the love of your life—in one moment. But don't mourn. Don't cry.
24.17: Stay silent. No funeral wailing. Keep your head wrapped. Put your shoes on. Don't eat nobody's comfort food."
24.18: So Ezekiel obeyed. In the morning he gave the message, and by that evening, his wife passed. And the next morning, he didn't shed a tear. Just did what God said.
24.19: The people were like, "Wait—what does all this mean? Why you actin' like this?"
24.21: 'Tell Israel: I'm about to desecrate what y'all hold dear—My temple. Y'all boast in it. Y'all call it your pride and joy. But I'ma take it. Just like that. And your sons and daughters gon' fall by the sword.
24.22: And just like I ain't mourned, you won't mourn either. No head coverings off, no sympathy meals.
24.23: Y'all gon' wear your turbans, keep your sandals on, and suffer quietly— not from grief over death, but from the weight of your sin.'
24.24: Ezekiel is your sign. What happened to me is what's gonna happen to y'all. When it goes down, then y'all will finally know—I'm the Lord."
24.25: "And you, son of man," God said, "On the day I take everything from them—their stronghold, their joy, their pride, their children—
24.26: someone who escapes the horror will come and tell you what happened.
24.27: And that day, I'ma let you speak freely again. You won't be mute no more. You'll be My sign. And they'll know exactly who I am."

25.1: The Lord came to Ezekiel and said,
25.3: Tell 'em this straight from Me: Y'all had the nerve to say 'Aha!' when My temple got wrecked, when Israel got wiped out, when Judah got hauled off in chains? Oh bet.
25.4: Because of that petty disrespect, I'm lettin' the folks from the East come through and take everything. They gon' set up camp in y'all land, live off your food, drink your milk, and do what they want.
25.5: I'ma turn your capital, Rabbah, into a camel garage, and all Ammon gon' be a pasture for sheep. Then y'all gon' know—I run this."
25.6: "Since you couldn't keep your hands to yourself—clappin', stompin', and celebratin' Judah's downfall like it was your win—
25.7: I'ma stretch My hand out against you, too. You about to be plundered, cut off, wiped out. Ain't nobody even gon' remember y'all like that no more. Then you'll know—I'm the Lord."

25.10: The same Easterners wreckin' Ammon? They takin' your land too. I'ma erase Ammon's name and let Moab watch it happen.
25.11: When I'm done judging y'all, you'll know who I am."
25.12: "Edom, you got way too comfortable swingin' back at Judah like this was some personal beef. You came at them with vengeance like you had somethin' to prove.
25.13: Now I'ma come for you—wipe out folks from Teman to Dedan. Y'all gon' be empty. No man, no beast.
25.14: And just so you feel it proper, I'ma let Israel be the one to run it back on you. My wrath, My fury—through them. Then you'll really know this ain't revenge—it's judgment."
25.15: "Philistines, y'all been salty for generations. That grudge you been holdin' turned into violence. You wanted to see Israel destroyed just 'cause you got old beef.
25.16: Well, now I'm bringin' the smoke. I'ma stretch out My hand and cut y'all off. Cherethites? Gone. That last lil' group of seacoast dwellers? Burnt out.
25.17: My rebuke ain't gon' be light—it's gon' be loud, fierce, and final. And when it hit, everybody gon' know—I AM the Lord."

26.1: It was the eleventh year, first day of the month, when the word from the Lord hit me again.
26.2: "Son of man, go on and check Tyre. They been talkin' slick, sayin', 'Aha! Look at Jerusalem, the gateway for all them folks—busted down. Now it's all mine. I'm finna get rich off her downfall.'"
26.3: God said, "Aight Tyre, bet. I'm comin' for you. I'm sendin' wave after wave of nations to hit you—just like the ocean hit the shore nonstop."
26.4: "They gon' tear down your walls, knock down your towers. I'ma scrape you bare—clean like a rock top with nothin' on it."
26.5: "You gon' be nothin' but a spot to dry fishnets out in the sea. I said it. It's gon' happen. You about to be free game for any nation that want a piece."
26.6: "All them little towns you got in the fields? Sword. Dead. Then folks will know—I'm the Lord."
26.7: "Here's what I'ma do," says the Lord. "I'm bringin' Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, king of kings. He comin' down from the north with an army so deep—horses, chariots, troops for days."
26.8: "Them daughter towns? Gone. He comin' with a siege—gonna build up walls, pile up dirt, come at you hard."
26.9: "He'll aim battering rams right at your walls, and axes finna swing till your towers fall flat."
26.10: "So many horses, the dirt they kick up gon' black out the sun. Your walls gon' be shakin' when he roll in, gates bustin' wide open like it's already over."
26.11: "He gon' stomp through your streets like they nothin'. People cut down left and right. All your big strong statues? Crashin'."
26.12: "They gon' rob you blind—take all your gold, all your goods, tear down your pretty houses. Then throw all that rubble—wood, stone, dirt—right into the sea."
26.13: "And them songs y'all love to play? Done. No harps. No music. Silence."
26.14: "I'ma make you flat like bare rock. Folks just gon' spread nets on you. You won't ever be rebuilt. I said it. Period."
26.15: "Listen, Tyre—when you fall, it's gon' shake the whole coastline. When your people scream, when blood get spilled, even the distant cities gon' feel it."
26.16: "All the sea captains and coastal bosses gon' step down from they thrones, toss off they designer fits, and throw on fear like clothes. They gon' sit in the dirt, shakin' nonstop, watchin' your downfall in disbelief."
26.17: "Then they gon' cry about you like this: 'Dang! Tyre gone? You used to run the sea—big name, big game, scarin' everybody. Now look at you—finished.'"
26.18: "Them coastlands gon' be spooked when you fall. Even the oceanfront cities gon' be shook by your exit."
26.19: "When I turn you into a ghost town, buried underwater, drowned in the deep like Atlantis,
26.20: I'ma drop you down with the dead—old ghosts in the pit, people long gone. You gon' be stuck down there, deep in the shadows where nobody lives. You ain't ever comin' back. Meanwhile, I'ma shine My glory in the land of the living."
26.21: "I'm makin' you a whole horror story. Folks might go lookin' for you, but you ain't gon' be found. You done," says the Lord God.

27.1: Then the word of the Lord came to me again.
27.2: "Son of man, I need you to sing a funeral song for Tyre."
27.3: Say this to Tyre, the port city sittin' out at sea, trading with all the coastlands: "The Lord God says—'Tyre, you out here braggin' talkin' 'I'm flawless, I'm fine, I'm all that.'"
27.4: "You sittin' way out in the ocean, and your builders done had you lookin' like a supermodel ship."
27.5: "They used the flyest fir trees from Mount Senir for your boards. Pulled a strong cedar from Lebanon for your mast."
27.6: "Oars? They carved those outta oaks from Bashan. Ashurite craftsmen decked your planks in ivory from Cyprus. Bougie."
27.7: "You had Egyptian linen embroidered on your sails. Blue and purple from Elishah wrapped around you like couture."
27.8: "Sidon and Arvad? They was your crew, rowin' for you. Your pilots? Straight scholars—sharp folk from your own city."
27.9: "The old heads and pros from Gebal? They patched you up tight. Every ship out there, with they whole crew, came through just to buy your goods."
27.10: "You had Persian, Lydian, and Libyan soldiers up in your army, suited up with shields and helmets. They made you look real important."
27.11: "Men from Arvad kept guard on your walls, Gammad soldiers held down your towers. Their shields? Posted up like trophies. Made you look polished."
27.12: "Tarshish was one of your main buyers—traded silver, iron, tin, and lead for your luxury goods."
27.13: "Javan, Tubal, and Meshech? They out here exchanging bronze and even human lives for your merchandise. Yeah, human trafficking."
27.14: "Togarmah sent you horses, war stallions, and mules."
27.15: "Dedan came with ivory tusks and ebony wood. You was real high-end."
27.16: "Syria dropped emeralds, purple cloth, embroidery, linen, coral, and rubies on you for your stuff."
27.17: "Even Judah and Israel came with wheat, millet, honey, oil, and balm."
27.18: "Damascus paid big for your goods too. Luxury items, wine from Helbon, clean white wool—they had tabs with you."
27.19: "Dan and Javan came back and forth, bringin' iron, cassia, and fragrant cane."
27.20: "Dedan sold you saddle blankets, fancy riding gear."
27.21: "Arabia and all the Kedar princes brought lambs, rams, and goats for trade—constant customers."
27.22: "Sheba and Raamah? They came with top-shelf spices, rare jewels, and gold."
27.23: "Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba's market cities, Assyria, Chilmad—all in your rotation."
27.24: "They sold you premium threads—purple, embroidery, chestfuls of fly garments, colorful rope, all stacked up in your stalls."
27.25: "The ships of Tarshish hauled your inventory everywhere. You were full, flashy, and floatin' proud out in the sea."
27.26: "But your own rowers steered you into dangerous waters. Then boom—an east wind snapped you in half, right in the ocean."
27.27: "Your whole squad—merchants, warriors, seamen, builders, everybody—you and your cargo? All gone. Drownin' the same day you sank."
27.28: "Even the coastlands gon' shake when your pilots start screamin' out in panic."
27.29: "Every sailor, every deckhand, every captain? They gon' abandon ship and stand on shore, watchin' it all go down."
27.30: "They gon' cry out loud for you, throw dust on their heads, roll around in ash like it's a full-on funeral."
27.31: "They'll shave their heads bald, wear sackcloth, and cry till their hearts break—straight ugly cryin'."
27.32: "They gon' chant this over you: 'Who else got taken out like Tyre? A city that sank right in the sea?'"
27.33: "You used to feed whole nations, Tyre. Rich folks and royalty stayed ballin' off your hustle."
27.34: "But now you lay broken in the deep. All that money, all that crew—gone."
27.35: "The island people watchin' in shock. Their kings? Shook, pale-faced, scared."
27.36: "Traders from all over gon' hiss when they hear about you. You'll be a ghost story now—no comeback, no rebuild, just gone forever."

28.1: Then God hit me with another word.
28.2: "Son of man, go talk to the prince of Tyre and say: 'This what the Lord God say— You got real full of yourself. You out here claimin', 'I'm a god. I sit on a divine throne, chillin' in the middle of the sea.' But nah, bruh, you just a man. You not God, even if your heart swears you one."
28.3: "You think you slicker than Daniel, huh? Ain't no secret you can't figure out, huh?"
28.4: "Yeah, you smart. You got strategy. You ran up a bag—gold, silver, vaults full. A whole empire off your trading game."
28.5: "But now that you rich, your head too big. You really think all that wealth make you untouchable?"
28.6: "So here's what the Lord God say: Since your heart out here actin' like it's divine…"
28.7: "I'ma bring in outsiders, some real ruthless folk. They comin' for your pretty little empire, Slicin' through all that wisdom you proud of. They gon' make you look dusty."
28.8: "You gon' fall hard— Straight into the pit. You gon' die like them other bodies floatin' in the sea."
28.9: "You still gon' talk tough to the one who killin' you? Still think you divine when your life on the line? Nah, you gon' be real human then."
28.10: "You gon' die like a stranger, unclean, By the hand of some foreigners. I said it. That's that."
28.11: Then God gave me another message.
28.12: "Son of man, sing this funeral song for the king of Tyre. Say: 'This what the Lord God says— You was the whole package— Wise, beautiful, flawless. Top-tier."
28.13: "You was in Eden, back in God's own garden. You had on every precious stone— Sardius, topaz, diamonds, beryl, onyx, jasper, sapphires, turquoise, emeralds, and gold. Even your jewelry had music in it. Custom made from day one."
28.14: "You was a cherub—God's own appointed one— posted up on God's mountain, strolling around fire like it was light work."
28.15: "You was perfect, from birth, Until that dirt crept in."
28.16: "Your hustle got too wild. You stayed movin' product, but all that traffic brought violence. So you sinned. God said, 'Out!' You ain't holy no more. I kicked you off the mountain and out the fire."
28.17: "Your ego got fed off your beauty. You let pride ruin your wisdom. So I snatched you down, threw you in front of kings, so everybody could see your downfall."
28.18: "You messed up the sacred spaces, with all your shady business. So I lit a fire from inside you— Burned you to ashes right there, right in front of everybody."
28.19: "Folks who used to roll with you? They shook. They ain't even know what to say. You a horror story now. You done. No reboot, no resurrection."
28.20: Then God gave me another word:
28.21: "Son of man, now turn to Sidon and speak against her."
28.22: "Tell Sidon: 'Look, I'm comin' for you,' says the Lord God. 'I'ma show out right in your city. When I drop judgment, you gon' know who I am.'"
28.23: "I'm bringin' disease. Blood in the streets. Bodies fallin' left and right. Swords comin' from every angle. You gon' know—I am the Lord."
28.24: "And Israel? Y'all ain't gon' be bothered no more by folks like Sidon—no more thorns in your side. Everybody gon' finally know I'm God."
28.25: "Here's what else the Lord God says: When I bring My people—Israel— back from all the places they were scattered, and show My glory through them in front of the whole world…"
28.26: "They gon' live safe again. Build houses. Plant vineyards. Feel secure. While I serve judgment to all the nations that hated on 'em. And they gon' finally know: I am the Lord their God."

29.1: On the twelfth day of the tenth month, in the tenth year, God gave me a word.
29.2: "Son of man, turn and face Pharaoh, king of Egypt. Speak against him and the whole land of Egypt."
29.3: "Say this to him: This what the Lord God say— 'I'm comin' for you, Pharaoh. You big sea monster, layin' up in your rivers, Actin' like you own the Nile. You walk around talkin' bout, 'This my river! I made it myself!'"
29.4: "Nah, I'm finna hook you in the jaw. Drag you out the water with all them fish hangin' off you. Y'all stuck together in pride, now y'all stuck together in judgment."
29.5: "I'm tossin' you into the desert, You and your little fishy crew. Y'all gon' dry out in the field— No one pickin' y'all up, no burial. Y'all just gon' be food for wild animals and vultures."
29.6: "Then Egypt gon' know I'm God. Y'all was supposed to be support for Israel, But you was flimsy, like a reed."
29.7: "When Israel tried to lean on you, You snapped. You messed up their shoulders. You made 'em stumble and break down even worse."
29.8: "So here's what the Lord God say: I'm sendin' a sword your way. Everything breathin'? Gotta go."
29.9: "Egypt gon' be nothing but ruins. Why? 'Cause Pharaoh ran his mouth sayin', 'I made this river myself.'"
29.10: "So yeah, I'm against you AND your river. Egypt gon' be empty and ruined from top to bottom— From Migdol to Syene, all the way to Ethiopia's border."
29.11: "Ain't nobody walkin' through it. No humans, no animals. It's gon' be a ghost town for forty years."
29.12: "Egypt gon' sit in the middle of all the other wastelands. Their cities? Wiped out like the rest. For forty years, I'ma scatter the Egyptians all over the world."
29.13: "But after that," says the Lord God, "When the forty years is up, I'ma bring Egypt back. I'ma let 'em return to Pathros— Back to where they started. But they not gon' be the same."
29.14: "They gon' be humbled. They'll be the least of the kingdoms now. Ain't never gon' rise up like they used to."
29.15: "They'll never be a superpower again. I'ma make sure of that. They done ruling over folks."
29.16: "And Israel? Y'all won't be lookin' to Egypt no more for backup. That relationship gon' remind you of how y'all turned on Me. But once it's all said and done— You'll know I'm the Lord God."
29.17: Fast forward to the twenty-seventh year, first month, first day— God dropped another word.
29.18: "Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon? He went all out on Tyre. His army worked till they was bald and bruised— And after all that, they ain't get nothin' out of it. No reward. No plunder."
29.19: "So this what the Lord God say: I'ma give Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar. He gon' take all their riches, Get paid back in full for the effort he put in for Me."
29.20: "Egypt is his paycheck. That war wasn't just his—it was My will, And he put in work."
29.21: "And in that day? I'ma raise up strength in Israel again. I'ma loosen your lips, Ezekiel, So you can speak again among the people. And they gon' know— I am the Lord."

30.2: "Son of man, I need you to prophesy. Say this: This what the Lord God says— 'Cry out loud, y'all! The day of reckoning comin'!'"
30.3: "'That day right around the corner— The Day of the Lord is near. It's gon' be dark like storm clouds. It's judgment time for the nations.'"
30.4: "'A sword is comin' for Egypt, And Ethiopia gon' feel the pain too. Folks gon' be slain in Egypt, Their wealth snatched, And their whole foundation shattered.'"
30.5: "'Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, all them mixed-up folks, Chub and everybody ridin' with Egypt— They all gon' fall by the sword too.'"
30.6: This what the Lord says: "The ones who hold Egypt up? They droppin' too. That arrogant power Egypt got? It's comin' down hard. From Migdol to Syene—everybody gettin' touched."
