30.7: "Egypt gon' be sittin' in ruins, Just like all them other wrecked countries. Her cities gon' look like ghost towns."
30.8: "Then they gon' know I'm the Lord— When I light Egypt on fire And wipe out all her little helpers."
30.9: "I'ma send messengers in ships that day, They gon' make them carefree Ethiopians panic. The same kind of fear Egypt feel? They gon' feel it too— It's definitely goin' down."
30.10: This what the Lord God says: "I'ma shut Egypt down. And I'ma use Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, to do it."
30.11: "Him and his people— They some cold-blooded warriors. They comin' to destroy Egypt. They drawin' swords And leavin' bodies everywhere."
30.12: "I'ma dry up the rivers, And sell the land off to evil folks. Foreigners gon' wreck it all— The land, the people, the cities. I'm the one sayin' it—don't get it twisted."
30.13: The Lord says this too: "I'ma destroy all them fake gods. I'ma shut down all them idols in Noph. Ain't gon' be no more rulers in Egypt— I'ma send fear through the whole land."
30.14: "Pathros? Wasteland. Zoan? Set on fire. No? Judgment comin'."
30.15: "Sin, the fortress of Egypt? I'ma pour My wrath there. No? Overcrowded no more— They gettin' cut down."
30.16: "Fire's comin' through the whole land. Sin gon' cry out in agony, No gon' be split open, Noph gon' be shook every single day."
30.17: "Young men in Aven and Pi Beseth? Killed in the streets. Them cities? Goin' into captivity."
30.18: "Even Tehaphnehes gon' lose its light. I'ma break the stronghold there. Egypt's pride? Gone. A cloud of sorrow gon' cover her, And her daughters gon' be taken captive."
30.19: "All this judgment I'm bringin'? Egypt gon' know— I'm the Lord."
30.20: On the seventh day of the first month, eleventh year—God dropped another word on me.
30.21: "Son of man, Pharaoh's arm? Yeah, I broke that. And it ain't even wrapped up or splinted. He too weak now to even hold a sword."
30.22: "So this what the Lord God say: 'I'm against Pharaoh. I'ma break both his arms— The strong one AND the one already messed up. He won't be holdin' no sword after that.'"
30.23: "I'ma scatter the Egyptians all over the map. Spread 'em out in every direction."
30.24: "But Babylon? I'ma strengthen him. I'ma put My sword in his hand. Pharaoh? Still weak—he gon' groan like a man Takin' his last breath on the battlefield."
30.25: "The king of Babylon gon' rise. Pharaoh gon' fall. And when they see My sword In Babylon's hand, And he pointin' it straight at Egypt— They gon' know I'm the Lord."
30.26: "I said it before, I'ma say it again— I'ma scatter the Egyptians. Send 'em runnin' in every direction. Then they'll know— I Am the Lord."

31.1: In the eleventh year, third month, first day, God came with another word.
31.2: "Son of man, speak to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and his whole crew: 'Who you think you matchin' in greatness?'"
31.3: "Let's talk about Assyria— That joint was like a cedar in Lebanon: Tall, fine branches, thick shade, Towerin' up high into the clouds."
31.4: "It was them deep waters that made it grow, Underground streams kept liftin' it up. Water flowed all around where it was planted, And lil' streams shot out to feed other trees in the field."
31.5: "That's why it grew taller than every other tree. Branches stretched far, Soakin' up all that water, Spreadin' wide."
31.6: "Birds nested in its branches, Wild animals chilled underneath, And all kinds of nations took shelter in its shade."
31.7: "It looked beautiful— Tall, wide, strong— Roots dipped into the deep waters."
31.8: "No cedar in Eden could even stand next to it. Fir trees? Nah. Chestnut trees? Not even close. No tree in God's garden could match its beauty."
31.9: "I made it dope with them long branches. Even the trees in Eden got jealous."
31.10: So here's what God says: "Since it got proud 'cause it stood so tall, And its heart swelled with pride,
31.11: I handed it over to a boss nation— Somebody ruthless. He chopped it down for all its evil ways."
31.12: "Foreign nations—mean ones— Came in and tore it apart. Branches fell in the mountains, Limbs got scattered in valleys and rivers. Everybody ran from under its shade— They ain't stick around."
31.13: "All that's left? Birds pickin' at what's left, Beasts crawlin' through the ruins."
31.14: "I did this to show: No tree planted by the water Should get too high and mighty again. Ain't none of them trees reachin' for the clouds anymore. 'Cause they all gon' end up the same— Dead. Laid out underground, With the rest of humankind, Down in the Pit."
31.15: God said: "When that tree fell, Even the underworld mourned. I made the waters stop flowin'. Lebanon cried over it, All the trees drooped in sadness."
31.16: "Whole nations trembled when it hit the ground. I threw it down to hell With all the others headed for the Pit. Even the trees of Eden—the finest ones— Felt some type of way, Like, 'Dang, even that tree ain't make it?'"
31.17: "That tree went to the grave With the ones killed by the sword. All the folks that once stood strong in its shadow— They in the dirt now too."
31.18: "So Pharaoh—let Me ask you this: Which tree in Eden do you really think you're like? Big, bad, glorious? Guess what— You goin' down just like they did. You and your whole squad Gon' be laid out with the rest of 'em, Down in the dirt, Uncircumcised, Cut down by the sword. That's Pharaoh and all his people." –The Lord God said it.

32.1: In the twelfth year, twelfth month, first day, God pulled up on me again with a word.
32.2: "Son of man, go ahead and write Pharaoh's eulogy. Say this: 'You thought you was a young lion out here with the nations? Nah, you was more like a sea monster— Stirrin' up the waters, Kickin' up mud, Foulin' everything you touched.'"
32.3: "This what God says: 'I'm throwin' a net over you, Whole crowd of folks gon' help Me drag you out.'"
32.4: "I'm leavin' you out in the open field, Birds pickin' at you, Wild animals feasting on you."
32.5: "Your body gon' be laid out on the mountains, Valleys filled with your flesh."
32.6: "Yo blood gon' run so deep, It'll water the land, Even fill up dry riverbeds."
32.7: "When I shut your light off, The sky gon' go dark. Stars won't shine, Sun gon' hide, Moon gon' stay out the picture."
32.8: "All the heavenly lights gon' dim on your land— Whole place gon' be in the dark."
32.9: "I'ma shake folks' hearts all over the world, When they hear about your downfall— Places that ain't never even heard of you before."
32.10: "Kings gon' be shook. Hands shakin', Faces pale, Scared for their lives when they see My sword swingin'."
32.11: "God said, 'The king of Babylon comin' with that blade.'"
32.12: "He got a savage army— Most feared outta all the nations— They gon' run through Egypt, Leave nothin' standin'."
32.13: "Even the animals by the Nile? Gone. No more muddy feet, no more trampled banks."
32.14: "I'ma let the waters calm again— Flowin' smooth like oil."
32.15: "When I wipe Egypt out, When the cities empty and silent, Then they gon' know: I'm the Lord."
32.16: "This the funeral song they gon' sing. Daughters from all over gon' be cryin' for Egypt— Mournin' her and her whole crew."
32.17: Two weeks later, same year— God spoke again:
32.18: "Son of man, cry out for Egypt's whole crew. Tell 'em they about to join the other dead nations, Down in the Pit."
32.19: "You thought you were beautiful? Go ahead—lay down with the rest of the uncircumcised."
32.20: "You gon' die like the rest, Sword takin' you and everybody with you."
32.21: "Even the mighty warriors in hell gon' notice you: 'There go Pharaoh—he down here with the rest of us.'"
32.22: "Assyria's already down here, Graves all around her, Everybody slain by the sword."
32.23: "She deep down in the Pit, Company all around, They brought terror to the world— Now they just bones."
32.24: "Elam's there too— Same thing: Fell by the sword, Uncircumcised, Now they sittin' in shame underground."
32.25: "Whole crew laid out together, Dead and disgraced. They scared folks when they were alive, But now they buried with the rest of the shameful."
32.26: "Meshech and Tubal—yeah, they here too. Bodies everywhere. Uncircumcised, dead by the sword. They were out there flexin', Now just more bones in the dark."
32.27: "They don't even get buried with honor. Their swords under their heads, But guilt still on they bones— Terror don't make you holy."
32.28: "Pharaoh, you right there with 'em. Laid out with the rest of the slain, Same sword that got them gon' get you too."
32.29: "Edom? Yup. Kings, princes—all of 'em. Once thought they were strong, Now they laid up with the uncircumcised in the Pit."
32.30: "Even the princes of the north— And the Sidonians— They brought terror too, But now they just another name on the dead list."
32.31: "Pharaoh gon' see all them other fallen kingdoms And feel a weird kinda comfort: 'Least I ain't fall alone.' But you still fallen though."
32.32: "I let folks fear My name while y'all were alive. Now Pharaoh and his whole crew Gon' lay right there with the rest of the dead, Uncircumcised, Cut down by the sword. That's how this ends." –God said it. Period.

33.1: God came through with another word.
33.2: "Son of man, go tell your people this: If I send trouble—like war or judgment— And the people post up a watchman from their own block,
33.3: And that watchman see danger comin', If he blow the trumpet and warn everybody,
33.4: Then if somebody hear it but ignore it— That's on them. If they get caught up, Their blood ain't on nobody but themself.
33.5: They heard the warning and still didn't move. They brought that on they own head. But if they listened? They woulda saved they own life.
33.6: Now if that same watchman see danger And keep quiet? Don't say nothin'? And somebody die 'cause they ain't get the heads-up? Yeah, they still gon' die in they sin— But I'm holdin' that watchman responsible. That's blood on his hands."
33.7: "So look, son of man—I made you that watchman. I talk, you better speak up. Tell the people what I said."
33.8: "If I say, 'Wicked man, you gon' die,' And you say nothin'? They gon' die in sin, But you gon' have to answer for that."
33.9: "But if you do warn them, And they still don't change? They'll die in their mess— But you? You good. You did your part."
33.10: "Now tell Israel this: Y'all always crying, 'Our sins too heavy! We dying out here—how we gon' live?'
33.11: Tell 'em: 'I ain't out here rootin' for death,' says the Lord. 'I don't want nobody out here dyin' in sin. I want y'all to change and live. Turn around! Turn around! Why y'all out here tryna die, Israel?'"
33.12: "Now break this down for 'em, son of man: Just 'cause you been righteous don't mean you untouchable If you turn around and wild out. Same way—if you been wicked, But switch up and do right, You ain't gotta fall with the past."
33.13: "If I tell the righteous, 'You good,' But they start trippin'? That past righteousness don't count no more. They gon' die in what they doin' now."
33.14: "But if I say, 'You gon' die,' And that wicked one turn they life around—"
33.15: "Return what they stole, Do right by folks, Follow the law and stop the sin— That person gon' live."
33.16: "None of that old dirt gon' count against them. They turned around. They did right. They gon' live."
33.17: "But your people be sayin': 'God not bein' fair!' Nah, they the ones bein' shady."
33.18: "If somebody do right but then turn to evil— They gon' die for it."
33.19: "But if somebody was wildin' out, And they get they act together— They gon' live."
33.20: "Y'all still wanna say I'm unfair? I'm judging everybody by what they do. Ain't no favorites."
33.21: Twelfth year of captivity. Tenth month. Fifth day. Somebody who escaped from Jerusalem ran up to me: "Yo… the city gone. It's taken."
33.22: But God already had me the night before— Opened my mouth again. So when that man showed up, I was finally able to speak again.
33.23: Then God dropped another word on me:
33.24: "Them folks who still chillin' in the ruins talkin' like, 'Abraham was one man and got the land— We plenty—we for sure get to keep it.'"
33.25: "Tell 'em this from Me: 'Y'all still out here eatin' bloody meat, Still lookin' to idols, Still killin' folks. Y'all think y'all deserve this land?'"
33.26: "Y'all trust in violence. Y'all dirty with sin. Y'all sleepin' with each other's wives. You really think you supposed to own this place?"
33.27: "Tell 'em: Everybody in the ruins? Sword gon' get 'em. Those out in the fields? Beasts gon' eat 'em. In caves and hideouts? Disease gon' find 'em."
33.28: "I'ma make this land quiet—real quiet. Y'all pride? Done. Mountains empty. Nobody walkin' through."
33.29: "When I turn it into a wasteland, Y'all gon' know— I am the Lord."
33.30: "Son of man, lemme tell you what's really goin' on: They talkin' about you behind closed doors. On the low they be like, 'Hey, come listen to this prophet. He be speakin' the word.'"
33.31: "They show up like fans, Sit down like they My people, Act real churchy… But they don't do nothin' I say. They all talk—hearts still chasin' money and self."
33.32: "To them, you just entertainment. Like some R&B singer with a pretty voice and nice beat. They vibe with the sound… But they don't move on the message."
33.33: "But when all this really happen— And it will— They gon' know: A prophet was talkin' to 'em the whole time."

34.1: God came with another word for me.
34.2: "Son of man, speak out against these so-called shepherds in Israel. Tell them: 'The Lord God got somethin' to say to y'all: Y'all supposed to be feedin' the flock, but instead y'all feedin' yourselves. Shame on you.'"
34.3: "Y'all eat good, rockin' the wool, livin' off the fat sheep— But ain't givin' nothing back to the ones you supposed to be takin' care of."
34.4: "Y'all ain't helped the weak. Ain't healed the sick. Ain't bandaged the broken. Ain't went after the ones that ran off or got lost. All y'all do is flex power and treat people cold."
34.5: "So the sheep ran off—scattered everywhere— And the wild beasts ate 'em up, 'Cause they ain't had nobody watchin' over them."
34.6: "My people out here lost, Wanderin' through mountains and high places, Spread all over the earth… And ain't nobody even lookin' for them."
34.7: "So listen up, you fake shepherds—God got a word."
34.8: "'I swear on My name,' says the Lord, 'Since y'all let My sheep become prey for every wild thing, And y'all didn't even try to find them— Just kept lookin' out for yourselves—'"
34.10: "'I'm comin' for y'all. I'm takin' My sheep out y'all hands. Y'all ain't gon' be able to eat off them no more. I'ma rescue My people from y'all mouths— Y'all won't be snackin' off their backs ever again.'"
34.11: "I'm tellin' y'all straight up," says the Lord, "I'm bout to go get My sheep Myself. I ain't waitin' on nobody no more."
34.12: "Like a real shepherd go find his scattered sheep— That's what I'm gon' do. I'm pullin' them out the dark clouds and confusion where they got lost."
34.13: "I'ma bring them back from all over the world, And I'm takin' them home to their land. They gon' eat good in the valleys and hills of Israel."
34.14: "They gon' have real food, Restin' in peace, Chillin' on mountaintop pastures. No more scraps."
34.15: "I, the Lord, gon' feed them Myself, And let them finally lay down and rest."
34.16: "I'm comin' for the lost ones. I'm bringin' back the ones who ran off. I'm patchin' up the wounded. Strengthenin' the sick. But the proud, the greedy? I'm comin' with judgment. They gettin' humbled."
34.17: "And now to y'all, My flock," says the Lord, "I'ma deal with y'all too. I'm gon' separate sheep from sheep—rams from goats."
34.18: "Y'all fat sheep done ate up the best grass And trampled the rest. You drink clean water And muddy up what's left for everybody else?"
34.19: "My other sheep gotta eat what y'all stepped on And drink the dirty leftovers. That ain't right."
34.20: "So I'ma step in," says the Lord. "I'm gon' judge between the fat and the skinny sheep."
34.21: "Y'all bullies pushin' folks with y'all sides and horns, Shovin' the weak ones out the way, Scatterin' the ones who need help."
34.22: "But I'ma save My flock. Ain't nobody gon' be prey no more. I'm holdin' everybody accountable."
34.23: "I'ma raise up one Shepherd for them— My servant David. He gon' feed them right. He gon' lead them how they supposed to be led."
34.24: "And I, the Lord, will be their God, And David gon' be their prince. I said what I said."
34.25: "I'm makin' a peace deal with them. No more wild animals tearin' them up. They gon' be safe in the wilderness, Sleepin' sound in the woods."
34.26: "I'ma bless them and everything around 'em. Rain gon' fall when it's supposed to. It's gon' be rain full of blessing."
34.27: "The trees gon' bear fruit. The land gon' give harvest. They gon' live safe and free."
34.28: "No more fear of enemies. No more beasts tearin' through. Just peace, safety, and freedom."
34.29: "I'ma plant a garden of fame for them— They'll be fed, respected, And won't be embarrassed by outsiders ever again."
34.30: "They gon' know I'm with them. No more guessin'. I'm their God, and they My people."
34.31: "Y'all My flock. The flock of My pasture. You just people, But I'm God. And I got y'all."

35.1: Then God came to me again with a word.
35.2: "Son of man, turn your face toward Mount Seir and speak this word over it."
35.3: "Tell it straight: The Lord God say, 'Mount Seir, I'm comin' for you. I'm stretchin' out My hand, and you gon' be left in ruins.'"
35.4: "Your cities? Gone. Your name? Wiped out. Then you gon' know—I'm the Lord."
35.5: "Why? 'Cause you been hatin' on Israel since forever. You shed blood like it was nothin', Especially when they were already down bad, Right when they was just tryna get back up."
35.6: "So hear Me when I say this," says the Lord God: "You loved blood? Cool. Now blood gon' chase you. I'm preparin' blood for you, And it won't stop comin'."
35.7: "Mount Seir gon' be desolate—real quiet, Ain't nobody comin' or goin'."
35.8: "Your mountains? Full of bodies. Your hills, your valleys, your low places? Covered in folk laid out by the sword."
35.9: "You gon' be permanently desolate. Ain't no one tryna move back there. Then you'll know—I am the Lord."
35.10: "You said in your heart, 'Both Israel and Judah? Yeah, we takin' that. It's ours now.' Like God ain't still up in there."
35.11: "So guess what," says the Lord, "I'ma pay you back with that same energy— That hate you had? That envy you moved in? Yeah, you gon' feel it. And My people gon' see who I really am When I judge you."
35.12: "You'll know I'm the Lord, 'Cause I heard every foul word you spit About the mountains of Israel. You was like, 'They done. That land ours now.'"
35.13: "You ran your mouth on Me, Talkin' bold like you run things. I heard everything."
35.14: "The whole world gon' throw a party When I leave you empty and cold."
35.15: "You was laughin' when My people lost everything— When their land was destroyed. Now I'ma flip the script. Mount Seir? You gettin' that treatment. You and all of Edom. And after that? You'll know who I am."

36.1: God told me, "Son of man, speak up to the mountains of Israel and say, 'Y'all better listen to what the Lord say.'"
36.2: This what the Lord God said: "Since your enemies had the nerve to shout, 'Aha! Them hills and heights we been wantin'? They ours now!'"
36.3: Go ahead and prophesy. Say: "Because folks came through, tore you up, took over from every side, and now all these nations run they mouths about you…"
36.4: So hear Me, mountains, hills, rivers, valleys, ruins, and deserted cities that everybody's been jokin' about and robbin'—this the word of the Lord.
36.5: I'm hot with jealousy for y'all. Edom and all the other nations took what's Mine with evil hearts and greedy hands—like it was free for the takin'.
36.6: So speak on it: Tell the land of Israel, 'God mad. He jealous. And yeah, He saw y'all carryin' the weight of everybody's shade.'
36.7: That's why I, the Lord, swear: them other nations gon' get clowned too. They gon' feel what shame really is.
36.8: But you? Mountains of Israel? You gon' grow again. Branches gon' shoot out, fruit gon' show up—for My people, Israel, 'cause they comin' home.
36.9: I'm with y'all now. I'm turnin' back toward you. Y'all gon' be worked, planted, and made beautiful.
36.10: I'ma multiply folks on you—all of Israel. The cities gon' be full again. The ruins? Rebuilt.
36.11: People, animals—everything gon' grow. Y'all gon' have more than you did before. And that's how you'll know I'm the Lord.
36.12: I'ma bring My people home to walk this land again. It's theirs now. You belong to them, not to loss.
36.13: The Lord said: "They used to say y'all chew up your own people and keep the nation from growin'…"
36.14: But that's over. No more eatin' up folks. No more takin' children or futures. That's done.
36.15: I won't let folks talk down on you no more. Ain't no more shame, no more disrespect. And no more stumblin' blocks in your own house."
36.16: Then God came to me with another word.
36.17: "Son of man, when Israel lived in their land, they messed it up with their ways. I saw it—dirty like a woman on her cycle, unclean through and through.
36.18: I got angry. Real angry. They spilled blood and worshipped idols. So I poured out My judgment.
36.19: I scattered them. Sent them all over the map. Judged 'em based on how they acted.
36.20: But even in exile, they embarrassed Me. People pointed and said, 'Ain't that God's people? Why He let 'em get kicked out like that?'
36.21: Still, I cared about My name. Yeah, they dragged it, but I ain't lettin' My name go out like that forever."
36.22: So tell Israel: "I ain't doin' this for you," says the Lord. "I'm cleanin' y'all up for My name's sake—'cause y'all been messin' it up everywhere y'all went."
36.23: "I'm about to make My name big again. The same name y'all profaned. But when I show out through y'all, The nations gon' know who I am."
36.24: "I'm bringin' y'all back—outta every land, every corner. Back to the place I gave your people."
36.25: "I'm gon' wash y'all clean. Y'all been filthy with idols and foolishness— But I'm rinsin' all that off."
36.26: "I'ma give you a brand new heart— One that's soft, not stone cold. And I'ma put a whole new spirit in you."
36.27: "My Spirit gon' live in you, And help you walk how I told y'all to walk. You'll finally live right."
36.28: "Then you gon' live in the land I promised your ancestors. You'll be My people. I'll be your God."
36.29: "I'ma save y'all from all that grime. Your crops gon' grow. Famine? Nah—we not doin' that again."
36.30: "Your trees gon' bear fruit. Your fields gon' flourish. Ain't no nation gon' clown y'all for bein' broke ever again."
36.31: "When all this hit, Y'all gon' look back and realize how triflin' y'all were— And it's gon' break your heart."
36.32: "Let Me make it clear again: I ain't doin' this 'cause y'all earned it. I'm doin' it so the world knows I'm God. Y'all should be ashamed, for real."
36.33: "But on that day I clean y'all up? Cities rebuilt. Ruins restored. It's up."
36.34: "That wasteland folks used to laugh at? It gon' look like Eden. People gon' walk by and say, 'Wait… wasn't this a dump? Now it's thrivin'?'"
36.35: "Ruins gon' become neighborhoods. Barren places gon' bloom."
36.36: "And all them other nations nearby? They gon' know I'm the one who flipped the script. I planted what was dead. I rebuilt what was lost."
36.37: "I'ma let y'all ask Me for this, too. And I'ma do it. I'ma multiply your people like a flock."
36.38: "Like the sacred flocks that filled Jerusalem on feast days, That's how your cities gon' look—full and alive again. And then? Everybody gon' know I'm the Lord."

37.1: The hand of the Lord came and scooped me up. His Spirit dropped me right in the middle of a valley full of dry bones.
37.2: He had me walk through it—bone after bone, scattered everywhere. And lemme tell you, they was real dry.
37.3: Then He asked, "Son of man, you think these bones can live again?" I said, "Lord… only You know that."
37.4: Then He said, "Speak to these bones. Say, 'Dry bones, listen to what the Lord gotta say!'"
37.5: "This is what God says to these bones: 'I'ma breathe life into y'all. Y'all gon' live again.'"
37.6: "I'ma hook the muscles back up, cover you with skin, and breathe into you—and you gon' come back to life. Then y'all gon' know I'm the Lord."
37.7: So I did what He said—I prophesied. And while I was speakin', I heard a rumblin', bones clickin' and clackin' back together—bone to bone.
37.8: Then I saw muscles form on 'em, skin coverin' 'em—but they still wasn't breathin'. No life just yet.
37.9: God said, "Now speak to the breath, son of man. Call it from all four winds. Tell it to come breathe on these dead ones so they can live."
37.10: I did what He said—and breath came in. They stood up on they feet, strong and ready. A whole army, lookin' like they never missed a beat.
37.11: Then God told me, "These bones? They Israel. They say, 'We dried up. Hope gone. We cut off.'"
37.12: "So tell 'em this: 'I'm about to open y'all graves, bring you back up, and take you home to Israel.'"
37.13: "When I open them graves and raise y'all up, then y'all gon' know it's Me—I'm the Lord."
37.14: "I'ma put My Spirit in you, and you gon' live. I'ma plant y'all right back in your land. And everybody gon' know I'm the one who said it—and did it."
37.16: He said, "Son of man, grab a stick and write on it: 'Judah and the people rollin' with him.' Then grab another stick and write: 'Joseph—Ephraim—and all his crew.'"
37.17: "Now put them two sticks together in your hand, like they one stick."
37.18: When folks ask, 'Yo, what this mean?'
37.19: Say, "God said He takin' Joseph's stick and Judah's stick, and He puttin' 'em together. One people. One hand. One God."
37.20: "Hold them sticks up so they can see it."
37.21: Then say, "This what God said: I'm bringin' My people back from all them places they got scattered to."
37.22: "I'ma make 'em one nation. No more North and South. No more split. One king gon' rule all of 'em."
37.23: "They ain't gon' mess with idols no more. No nasty stuff. No foolishness. I'ma clean 'em up. They gon' be My people, and I'ma be their God."
37.24: "David My servant gon' be their king—one shepherd for everybody. They gon' live right, follow My Word, and do what I said."
37.25: "They gon' live in the land I gave Jacob. They kids, and they kids' kids, gon' stay there forever. David still gon' be prince over 'em forever too."
37.26: "I'ma make a peace deal with 'em. A forever covenant. I'ma multiply them, bless them, and plant My holy house right in the middle of 'em—forever."
37.27: "I'll be with them, livin' with them. They'll be My people. I'll be their God."
37.28: "Then the nations gon' know I'm the one who made Israel holy, when My presence is right there with 'em. Not once in a while—forevermore."

38.1: The word of the Lord came to me again.
38.2: "Son of man, turn your face toward Gog from the land of Magog—the big dog prince over Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal—and call him out."
38.3: "Tell him this what God said: 'Gog, I'm comin' for you. Yeah, you. Prince of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal.'"
38.4: "I'ma turn you around, drag you out with hooks in your jaw. You and your whole army—on horses, geared up in armor, shields, swords, the whole nine."
38.5: "Persia, Ethiopia, and Libya rollin' with you—all of 'em strapped and suited."
38.6: "Gomer and Togarmah bringin' their crews from the north too. You got a whole squad deep behind you."
38.7: "Get ready. Arm up. You and your whole camp. Be on standby."
38.8: "After a long while, you gon' show up. In the last days, you gon' come into the land of My people—the ones I brought back from war and exile. That land used to be empty, but now it's full again. They livin' peaceful."
38.9: "You gon' ride in like a storm, deep and heavy, like a cloud coverin' the land—your whole army with you."
38.10: God says, "When that day come, you gon' start thinkin' slick. Evil gon' start bubbling in your mind."
38.11: "You'll be like, 'I'm bout to hit these folks livin' in peace. No gates, no walls—they wide open.'"
38.12: "You tryna run up and rob 'em, snatch what they got. These the same folks I gathered from all over, who rebuilt the land and settlin' in, finally blessed with stuff again."
38.13: "Even Sheba, Dedan, Tarshish, and all their lil homies gon' say, 'Oh, you came to loot, huh? Tryna snatch gold, silver, cattle and goods?'"
38.14: "So son of man, speak this to Gog: When My people chillin' and livin' safe, don't act like you ain't know."
38.15: "You gon' ride down from the deep north—Gog and all your people—on horses, lookin' like an unstoppable force."
38.16: "You gon' storm Israel like a cloud in the end times. But guess what? I'm the one bringin' you there, so when I handle you, the world gon' know who I am."
38.17: "Ain't you the one I told the prophets about way back? They said somebody like you was comin'… and here you go."
38.18: "And when you touch down in Israel? That's when My fury gon' show up."
38.19: "I'm jealous for My people, and My anger burn hot. That day gon' shake the earth—a massive earthquake in Israel."
38.20: "Everything gon' feel it: fish in the sea, birds in the sky, animals, bugs, and every single person on earth. Mountains fallin', cliffs crumblin', every wall breakin' down."
38.21: "I'ma make chaos hit your camp. Folks gon' turn on each other—every man tryna survive, even if it mean stabbin' his brother."
38.22: "I'ma drop judgment on you: plague, bloodshed, heavy rain, hail, fire, and brimstone straight from the heavens."
38.23: "I'ma make sure the world see My greatness, feel My holiness. And when I'm done? All the nations gon' know: I AM the Lord."

39.1: "Alright now, son of man—go speak on Gog again. Tell him what the Lord God say: 'I'm still on your head, Gog—ruler of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal.'"
39.2: "I'm gon' drag you back from way up north and set you right in front of My people on Israel's mountains."
39.3: "Then I'ma slap that bow right out yo' left hand, and your arrows? They hittin' the dirt outta your right."
39.4: "You gon' fall, right there on them mountains—your whole squad with you. I'm feedin' y'all to the birds and wild animals like a feast."
39.5: "Ain't gon' be no burial. Y'all gon' die in the open field. Why? Cuz I said so," says the Lord.
39.6: "Oh and I ain't just stoppin' with you—I'm sendin' fire to Magog and all them chillin' in safety on them coastlines. When I'm done, everybody gon' know I'm the Lord."
39.7: "My holy name? Yeah, I'm gon' make it ring loud in Israel again. They ain't gon' mess with My name no more. And the nations? They gon' recognize I'm the Holy One in Israel."
39.8: "It's goin' down. Best believe it. I said it, and it's already in motion."
39.9: "Folks in Israel gon' come out and burn all y'all leftover weapons—shields, bows, spears, whatever—using it for firewood for seven years."
39.10: "They won't even need to chop trees no more. Just burn the weapons of war. And the same folks who got robbed? They gon' be the ones doin' the robbin' now," says the Lord.
39.11: "On that day, I'ma give Gog a gravesite in Israel—a valley east of the sea. It's gon' block the road 'cause that's where his whole crew get buried. They gon' call it Hamon Gog Valley."
39.12: "Israel gon' be buryin' bodies for seven straight months just to clean the land."
39.13: "Everybody gon' take part in it, and that act alone? That's gon' give 'em some clout when I show out and get My glory," says the Lord.
39.14: "They even gon' hire folks just to do clean-up duty—lookin' for bones and settin' markers."
39.15: "When the crew find a bone, they'll flag it till the bury team come scoop it up and drop it in Hamon Gog Valley."
39.16: "Even the city nearby gon' be called Hamonah. That land gon' be clean after that."
39.17: "And you, son of man, tell the birds and beasts this: 'Y'all better pull up. I got a feast for y'all—God's own barbecue on Israel's mountains.'"
39.18: "Feast on the mighty ones, drink blood of earth's top dogs—rams, lambs, bulls, goats—all them fattened up in Bashan."
39.19: "Eat till you stuffed, drink till you gone off it—it's God's sacrifice, and it's all laid out."
39.20: "Horses, riders, soldiers, war men—you gon' be full off all them. This My table," says the Lord God.
39.21: "Then I'ma flex My glory across the nations. Everybody gon' witness the judgment I drop and know I did that."
39.22: "From that day forward, Israel gon' know—I am their God."
39.23: "Even the Gentiles gon' understand why Israel got dragged into exile. It wasn't random—it was cuz they was unfaithful. So I hid My face, let their enemies handle them."
39.24: "I dealt with them based on their dirt. I ain't sugarcoated nothin'."
39.25: "But now? I'ma bring back Jacob's people. I'm showin' mercy on all of Israel. I'm protecting My holy name."
39.26: "Yeah, they carried their shame and all that betrayal when they lived comfy and forgot Me—but I'm still gon' step in."
39.27: "I'ma gather 'em from all the lands I scattered 'em to. I'ma pull up in glory in front of all them other nations."
39.28: "That's when they gon' know I'm really their God—the One who sent 'em into exile, and the One who brought 'em home. Not a single one left behind."
39.29: "And I ain't hidin' My face no more. I'm pourin' out My Spirit on Israel. That's on Me," says the Lord God.

40.1: "25 years deep in exile, start of the year, tenth day of the month—14 years after Jerusalem fell—God pulled up on me again. Same day, His hand was on me heavy."
40.2: "In a vision, God took me back to Israel. He placed me on a real high mountain. Down south on that mountain? I saw somethin' that looked like a city."
40.3: "He brought me closer, and there was this man—glowin' like bronze. Had a measuring stick and linen tape in his hand. Bro posted up right at the gate."
40.4: "He told me, 'Son of man, open your eyes and ears. Pay close attention to everything I'm about to show you. You ain't here by accident—I brought you here to go back and tell Israel what's what.'"
40.5: "I saw a wall all the way around the outer edge of the temple. That man's stick was six cubits long (each cubit was a little longer than usual). He measured the wall—one rod high, one rod thick."
40.6: "Then we walked to the east gate. He went up the steps and measured the front part—one rod wide. Same on both sides."
40.7: "Each little side room in the gate was one rod by one rod. Five cubits in between 'em. That front part of the gate inside? One rod."
40.8: "He measured that inner vestibule too—one rod deep."
40.9: "That front vestibule space? Eight cubits. The gateposts? Two cubits. The entryway was inside the gate structure."
40.10: "East gate had three side rooms on each side—same size. Gateposts matched too."
40.11: "He measured the entrance—ten cubits wide. Full gate length? Thirteen cubits."
40.12: "There was a buffer zone in front of the rooms—one cubit on both sides. The side rooms themselves? Six cubits each."
40.13: "He checked the width from roof to roof of the opposite rooms—25 cubits wide. Doors facing each other directly."
40.14: "He measured the gateposts—60 cubits high. The whole court around the gate extended up to them."
40.15: "From the start of the outer gate to the start of the inner gate's vestibule? 50 cubits."
40.16: "I saw window openings around all the gate rooms and archways, shaped at an angle. Same with the vestibules—windows all around inside. And they carved palm trees on each gatepost."
40.17: "He brought me into the outer courtyard. All around it were rooms and a pavement floor. 30 rooms opened up to that walkway."
40.18: "The walkway ran next to the gates—same length as the gates. That was the lower pavement area."
40.19: "Then he measured the space from the outer gate front to the front of the inner court wall—100 cubits across, both toward the east and the north."
40.20: "We went to the north gate in the outer court. He measured its length and width."
40.21: "Three rooms on each side, plus gateposts and arches—same measurements as the east gate. Gate was 50 cubits long, 25 wide."
40.22: "Windows and palm tree carvings matched the east gate too. Seven steps led up to it. Archway right in front."
40.23: "There was a gate to the inner court straight across from this one—just like the east gate. Distance between gates? 100 cubits."
40.24: "Then we hit the south side. There was a gate there too, facing south. He measured the gateposts and arches—same layout."
40.25: "Windows all around, just like the others. Gate was 50 cubits long, 25 wide."
40.26: "Seven steps led up to this one too, with the archway in front. Palm tree carvings on each post—left and right."
40.27: "Another gate to the inner court, also facing south. Distance from gate to gate? 100 cubits."
40.28: "Now we entered the inner court through the south gate. He measured that too—same specs as the outer gates."
40.29: "Rooms, posts, arches—all measured the same. Windows all around. Length was 50 cubits, width was 25."
40.30: "The archways stretched 25 cubits long, five cubits wide—all around."
40.31: "These inner arches faced the outer court. Palm trees on the gateposts again. This one had eight steps going up."
40.32: "He took me to the inner east gate next. Same measurements."
40.33: "Rooms, posts, arches—same style. Windows all around. Gate was 50 long, 25 wide."
40.34: "Arches faced the outer court. Palm tree carvings again. Eight steps led up."
40.35: "Then we moved to the north inner gate. Measured just like the rest."
40.36: "Rooms, gateposts, arches—all had windows. 50 cubits long, 25 wide."
40.37: "Gateposts faced the outer court. Palm trees on both sides. Eight steps up."
40.38: "There was a room at the gatepost where they washed the burnt offerings."
40.39: "Inside the vestibule were four tables—two on each side—to kill the burnt, sin, and guilt offerings."
40.40: "As you walked toward the north gate entry, there were two more tables. And two more on the other side—same setup."
40.41: "So that's four on one side, four on the other—eight total for slaughterin' the sacrifices."
40.42: "There were also four stone tables, each 1.5 cubits square and one cubit high. That's where they laid the tools for cutting the meat."
40.43: "Hooks were attached inside—one hand wide—all the way around. And the meat? It sat right on the tables."
40.44: "Outside the inner gate, in the inner court, were two rooms for the singers—one on the south side of the north gate, the other on the north side of the south gate."
40.45: "Dude said, 'This south-facing room? That's for the priests over the temple.'"
40.46: "'And the north-facing room? That's for the priests who serve at the altar—Zadok's sons, from Levi's crew, the only ones allowed to step close to God.'"
40.47: "He measured the inner courtyard—100 cubits long, 100 cubits wide. It was a perfect square. The altar sat right in front of the temple."
40.48: "Then we pulled up to the temple porch. He measured the side posts—five cubits on each side. Gateway was three cubits wide on both sides."
40.49: "The porch itself was 20 cubits long, 11 cubits wide. Steps led up to it, and on each side of the doorway stood a pillar."

41.1: Then we stepped inside the main sanctuary. He measured the doorposts—six cubits thick on both sides. That's the width of the holy setup right there.
41.2: The doorway itself? Ten cubits wide. Each side wall of the entrance was five cubits thick. Whole room was 40 cubits long, 20 wide.
41.3: He went deeper and checked the next doorway—posts were two cubits thick. Entrance stood six cubits tall, and the doorway itself was seven cubits wide.
41.4: He measured the next room—20 cubits long and 20 wide, behind the main sanctuary. He looked at me and said, 'This right here? This the Most Holy Place.'
41.5: He checked the outer wall of the temple—six cubits thick. All around it, there were side rooms, each four cubits wide.
41.6: There were three levels of side rooms stacked on top of each other—30 rooms per level. The rooms sat on little ledges built into the temple wall. They ain't attach directly to the main wall, just rested on support ledges.
41.7: Each level went up like stairs—the higher up you went, the wider the rooms got 'cause of how the walls stepped out. The middle level led you from bottom to top.
41.8: I noticed the whole temple sat up on a platform. Foundation under the side rooms was six cubits tall—one full measuring rod.
41.9: The outer wall around the side rooms was five cubits thick. Then there was still a little space left around the edge of the temple—like a narrow terrace.
41.10: There was a 20 cubit-wide gap between that and the outer wall chambers, running all around the temple.
41.11: The side rooms had doors that opened into the terrace—one door facing north, one south. That terrace was five cubits wide all the way around.
41.12: Behind the temple, on the west end, there was a separate building. It was 70 cubits wide, walls five cubits thick, and it stretched 90 cubits long.
41.13: He measured the main temple—100 cubits long. Then the courtyard and that back building with its walls? Another 100 cubits.
41.14: Even the front of the temple, facing east with that courtyard? 100 cubits wide.
41.15: He checked the building out back that faced the courtyard, with its side porches—100 cubits. Same for the inner sanctuary and porch area.
41.16: Everything had doorposts and carved window frames. All around—three levels of galleries opposite the thresholds. Wood paneling ran from the floor all the way up to the windows—and yeah, the windows were covered.
41.17: From the top of the doors to the inner rooms, and on every single wall inside and out, everything was measured and set just right.
41.18: The place was decked out with carved cherubim and palm trees. One palm tree between each pair of cherubs. Every cherub had two faces.
41.19: One face looked like a man facing a palm, the other looked like a young lion, facing the other palm. That same design wrapped all the way around the temple.
41.20: From the floor to the top of the doorway, cherubim and palm trees covered the sanctuary walls.
41.21: The doorposts to the sanctuary were square-shaped, just like the front of the holy spot. All of it matched.
41.22: There was a wooden altar—three cubits high, two cubits long. Corners, length, and sides all made from wood. He told me, 'This the table that sits before the Lord.'
41.23: The temple and the Most Holy Place each had a set of double doors.
41.24: Each door had two folding panels—two panels per door, one set on each side.
41.25: Just like the walls, those doors had cherubim and palm trees carved in. And there was a wood canopy stretched over the porch area outside.
41.26: Window frames were beveled, and palm trees were on both sides of the porch—on the side rooms and up on the canopy too.

42.1: Then he took me back out to the outer court—on the north side—and brought me to some rooms sittin' across from the courtyard that separates the holy from the common. These rooms faced north, right near that other building.
42.2: These rooms were 100 cubits long and 50 cubits wide, with a door facing the north.
42.3: They sat opposite the inner court that was 20 cubits wide, and also across from the outer court pavement. You had stacked galleries—three levels high—one in front of the other.
42.4: Out front was a walkway 10 cubits wide, with a little one cubit space in between. All the doors faced north.
42.5: But up top? The upper rooms were smaller 'cause them gallery ledges cut into the space more than they did for the bottom and middle levels.
42.6: Since these rooms had three levels but no support pillars like the ones in the courts, the upper floor had to shrink in from the ground up.
42.7: There was a wall running in front of the rooms, parallel to 'em, facing the outer court—50 cubits long.
42.8: So the outer-facing rooms were 50 cubits long, while the ones facing the temple stretched 100 cubits.
42.9: There was an entrance to the lower rooms on the east side—you'd walk in from the outer court.
42.10: Now there were also rooms built right into the thickness of the outer wall on the east side—same placement as the north ones, opposite the separated courtyard and building.
42.11: These rooms had the same setup—same length and width, same look, same entrances and exits. They mirrored the ones to the north.
42.12: Just like the rooms that faced south, these had a doorway in front of the walkway, lined up with the eastern wall.
42.13: Then he broke it down for me: 'These north and south rooms, across from the sacred courtyard? That's where the priests go to eat the most holy offerings.'
42.14: 'They gon' store the grain offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings in there—it's sacred space. When the priests go in, they can't just walk back out into the outer court wearing them holy garments. Nah—they gotta change outta that sacred gear before stepping out to deal with the people.'
42.15: After he finished measuring the inside of the temple, he took me back out through the east gate. Now he was measuring the whole area all the way around.
42.19: Then he wrapped around to the west—yep, 500 rods there too.
42.20: He measured all four sides. And surrounding everything was a big wall—500 cubits by 500 cubits—set up to separate what's holy from what ain't.

43.1: After that, he brought me back to the east-facing gate.
43.2: And boom—here come the glory of the God of Israel, rollin' in from the east. His voice? Sounded like a whole ocean movin'. The earth lit up with His presence.
43.3: It hit me like the same vision I saw when I first came to announce judgment on the city. Same vibe I caught by the River Chebar. I hit the ground—face down.
43.4: God's glory entered the temple straight through that east gate.
43.5: The Spirit scooped me up and dropped me in the inner court. And just like that—the whole temple was flooded with the glory of the Lord.
43.6: Then I heard Him speakin' to me from inside the temple, and the man was still standin' next to me.
43.7: He said, 'Son of man, this right here? This My throne. My footstool. This where I'm settin' up shop, livin' with My people Israel—forever. Ain't gon' be no more disrespectin' My name. No kings, no folks, nobody draggin' My name through the mud with their little side gods and shady worship.'
43.8: 'They had the nerve to build their front doors right next to Mine, only a wall in between. They dirtied My holy name with all the mess they did. That's why I had to come down on 'em.'
43.9: 'But now? They need to toss all that foolishness and them dead kings outta My sight. Then I'll come dwell with them for good.'
43.10: 'Son of man, show the people what this temple look like. Let it hit 'em in the heart. If they feel shame for how they been livin', that's a start.'
43.11: 'If they really bout that repentance life, then show 'em every detail—how it's built, the ins and outs, all the rules, every line of the blueprint. Write it down in front of 'em so they can follow it for real.'
43.12: 'This the main rule: The whole mountaintop around the temple? It's extra holy. Don't get it twisted—this ain't regular ground. This the law of the temple.'
43.13: 'Now let's talk altar. Here go the measurements, using a long cubit (a regular cubit plus a handbreadth): The base is one cubit high and one cubit wide, with a little ledge—one span—around it.'
43.14: 'From the base to the first ledge is two cubits. That ledge? One cubit wide. Then from there to the next ledge is four cubits, and that one's also one cubit wide.'
43.15: 'The main altar top (the hearth) is four cubits tall. It got four horns reachin' up from the corners.'
43.16: 'The hearth itself is a perfect square—twelve cubits by twelve.'
43.17: 'The ledge around it is fourteen cubits long and wide. There's a rim around that—half a cubit high—and the base of the altar is one cubit all the way around. Steps goin' up face the east.'
43.18: Then He told me, 'Son of man, this what the Lord God says: Here go the rules for the altar once it's built and ready to use for burnt offerings and blood rituals.'
43.19: 'First, give a young bull to the Zadokite priests from Levi's tribe—the ones allowed to approach Me. That bull gon' be the sin offering.'
43.20: 'Take some of its blood, put it on the four horns of the altar, the corners of the ledge, and the rim all around it. That's how you cleanse and cover it.'
43.21: 'Then burn the bull at the designated spot outside the temple—but still inside holy grounds.'
43.22: 'Day two? Bring a goat with no blemishes for another sin offering. Cleanse the altar same way you did on day one.'
43.23: 'After that's done, bring in a young bull and a flawless ram.'
43.24: 'Put 'em before Me, throw salt on 'em, and offer them up as burnt offerings. Salt mean covenant—don't forget that.'
43.25: 'For seven straight days, y'all gon' bring a goat daily for a sin offering. Same with a bull and a ram—both spotless.'
43.26: 'Seven days straight they gon' purify that altar, atone for it, and make it holy.'
43.27: 'Then on the eighth day and from then on, the priests can offer burnt offerings and peace offerings for the people on that altar. And I'll receive y'all with open arms,' says the Lord God.

44.1: Then He brought me back to the outer gate of the sanctuary—the one that faces east—but guess what? It was shut tight.
44.2: And the Lord said, 'Leave it shut. Don't open it. Ain't nobody walkin' through it, 'cause the God of Israel already came through there. That gate been touched by glory—it stay closed.'
44.3: Now the prince? He got privilege. Since he's the prince, he can come sit inside the gate and eat bread in front of the Lord. But he gotta come in through the vestibule and leave the same way.
44.4: He brought me through the north gate to the front of the temple. And boom—God's glory was floodin' the place again. I hit the ground, face to the floor.
44.5: Then the Lord said, 'Listen close, son of man. Watch everything. Hear everything. I'm about to break down all the laws and rules for My house. Pay attention to who gets to come in and who gotta stay out.'
44.6: Go speak to these rebellious folks in Israel. Tell 'em: 'God said, enough with all the nasty stuff y'all been doin' in My house!'
44.7: 'Y'all brought in outsiders—uncircumcised in heart and body—folks who don't even respect Me—and let them come into My sanctuary and disrespect it. Gave 'em access to My table like it was nothin'. Y'all broke My covenant behind that foolishness.'
44.8: 'You didn't guard My sacred things. You let other folks handle My temple like it was just a job. Nah.'
44.9: 'From now on, no outsider—nobody with an uncircumcised heart or flesh—can enter My sanctuary. I don't care if they livin' in Israel or not.'
44.10: 'Now about them Levites who dipped out on Me when the people fell off, chasin' after idols—they gon' carry that guilt.'
44.11: 'I'll still let 'em serve in the temple—like security guards and assistants. They can handle sacrifices and help the people, but that's it.'
44.12: 'They stood with the people in their idol worship and helped lead them into sin. So I swore an oath—they gon' be held accountable.'
44.13: 'They not allowed to come close to Me, not as priests. They ain't touchin' My holy things or steppin' into the Most Holy Place. They gon' carry their shame.'
44.14: 'But I'll still let 'em manage temple duties—just not the sacred stuff.'
44.15: 'But the priests from the line of Zadok? They stayed loyal when everybody else fell off. They gon' be the ones that come close to Me. They gon' handle My fat and blood offerings.'
44.16: 'They can enter My sanctuary, step to My table, and carry out My commands.'
44.17: 'When they enter the inner court, they gotta wear linen—no wool, nothing hot or sweaty.'
44.18: 'Linen turbans, linen pants. No sweat-stained gear in My presence.'
44.19: 'When they step back out to the people in the outer court, they gotta change outta them holy clothes—leave them in the sacred rooms—and put on regular clothes. Ain't nobody supposed to catch a blessing just by brushing up against their ministry clothes.'
44.20: 'They can't shave their heads bald, but they can't let it grow wild either. Keep it neat, trimmed up.'
44.21: 'No wine when they come into the inner court. Stay sober before Me.'
44.22: 'They can't marry just anybody. No divorced women, no random widows. Only virgins from Israel or widows of other priests.'
44.23: 'They gon' teach My people what's holy and what ain't. Show 'em what's clean and unclean.'
44.24: 'When there's drama, they gon' be the ones to judge it—by My standards, not their own. They gon' hold it down on the Sabbaths and all My feast days too.'
44.25: 'They can't go near dead bodies and risk defilement—unless it's immediate family: mom, dad, child, brother, or an unmarried sister.'
44.26: 'Even then, after they touch death, they gotta wait seven days to get clean again.'
44.27: 'And when they come back to serve in the sanctuary? They gotta bring a sin offering. That's protocol,' says the Lord God.
44.28: 'Now let's talk inheritance. They ain't gettin' land like the rest of Israel. Why? 'Cause I'm their inheritance. I'm their portion.'
44.29: 'They get to eat the grain offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings. All the stuff dedicated to Me? It belongs to them.'
44.30: 'They get the best of all firstfruits and every kind of offering. You even gotta give 'em the first scoop of your flour to bless your house.'
44.31: 'But they ain't touchin' nothin' that died on its own or got ripped up by wild animals. That's off-limits.'

45.1: Now when y'all split the land for inheritance, set aside a district just for the Lord—a holy spot. It should be 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 wide. That whole area gon' be sacred.
45.2: Inside that space, there's a square for the sanctuary—500 by 500 rods—with 50 cubits of open space around it.
45.3: That whole district gon' be measured out: 25,000 long, 10,000 wide. Right there's where the sanctuary gon' sit—the Most Holy Place.
45.4: That holy section belong to the priests—the ones who serve up close to God. They'll live there, build their homes there, and take care of the sanctuary.
45.5: Then another 25,000 by 10,000 section go to the Levites, who handle temple work. They'll have 20 rooms in their spot.
45.6: Next to the holy district, give the city a section—5,000 cubits wide, 25,000 long. That's for all the people of Israel.
45.7: The prince gon' get land too—one side on the west, the other on the east of the holy district and city. His land stretch all the way across, from the west border to the east.
45.8: That land gon' be his territory. And My princes? They ain't gon' oppress My people no more. Let Israel live in peace, each tribe in their own part.
45.9: 'Enough of the nonsense, O princes of Israel!' says the Lord God. 'Cut out the violence, stop robbin' folks. Do right. Live righteous. And quit stealin' land from My people.'
45.10: 'Use honest scales, honest measurements—no funny business.'
45.11: 'The ephah and the bath should match—each one a tenth of a homer. Don't play games with the math.'
45.12: 'A shekel is 20 gerahs. Your money system? 20, 25, and 15 shekels add up to a mina.'
45.13: 'Here's what y'all owe the Lord: from every homer of wheat and barley, give one-sixth of an ephah.'
45.14: 'For oil, give one-tenth of a bath from every kor (that's ten baths or one homer).'
45.15: 'From every flock of 200 in the best pastures, give one lamb. That's for the grain, burnt, and peace offerings—to cover y'all,' says the Lord God.
45.16: 'Everybody in the land gotta give this offering for the prince.'
45.17: 'And the prince? He's responsible for the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings at the feasts, New Moons, Sabbaths, and all Israel's special days. He's the one who brings the sacrifices to make things right with God for the people.'
45.18: 'In the first month, on the first day, get a young bull with no flaws and purify the sanctuary.'
45.19: 'The priest will take some of that bull's blood and smear it on the temple doorposts, the altar corners, and the inner gateposts.'
45.20: 'Do the same thing again on the seventh day of that month—for anybody who sinned without knowin' or slipped up. That's how you cleanse the temple.'
45.21: 'On the fourteenth day of the first month, keep the Passover—seven-day feast, unleavened bread only.'
45.22: 'The prince gon' offer a bull as a sin offering—for himself and for everybody else in the land.'
45.23: 'Then each of the seven days, he gon' bring seven bulls and seven rams—no blemish—for burnt offerings. And each day, a goat too, for sin.'
45.24: 'He also brings a grain offering—one ephah for each bull, one ephah for each ram, and a hin of oil with each ephah.'
45.25: 'Then in the seventh month, on the fifteenth day, for the big feast? Same routine. Seven days straight. Sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain, oil—all of it lined up right.'

46.1: God said, "Alright, listen. That inner courtyard gate that faces east? Keep it locked up six days out the week. But come Sabbath or New Moon? Open that thing up."
46.2: "The prince gon' roll in from the outer entrance and stand by the gatepost. The priests gon' do their thing—burnt offerings, peace offerings. He gon' worship from the threshold, then dip. Gate stays open till sundown."
46.3: "Same for the people—they gon' pull up at that eastern gate and worship too on Sabbaths and New Moons."
46.4: "On the Sabbath, the prince gotta bring six flawless lambs and one perfect ram for the burnt offering."
46.5: "He also gotta bring a grain offering—one ephah for the ram, and as much as he wanna give for the lambs. Plus a splash of oil—one hin per ephah."
46.6: "On New Moon days, he better show up with a flawless young bull, six lambs, and one ram—all without blemish."
46.7: "Same deal—one ephah for the bull, one for the ram, as much grain as he wants for the lambs, and a hin of oil for each ephah."
46.8: "When the prince comes in, he gotta use the vestibule route—and leave the same way he came in."
46.9: "Now when the people come through for the feast days, if you enter from the north gate, you gotta leave out the south gate. And vice versa. Don't leave the same way you came in."
46.10: "And when the folks come in and go out, the prince gon' move with them—same entrance, same exit."
46.11: "At these special feast days, the grain game stays the same: one ephah for a bull, one for a ram, as much as he wants for the lambs, and that hin of oil per ephah."
46.12: "Now if the prince wanna pull up with a voluntary burnt or peace offering? Let him. Open that east gate for him like it's Sabbath. Once he done and walks out, close that gate behind him."
46.13: "Every single morning, bring a flawless one-year-old lamb to the Lord as a burnt offering. No skips."
46.14: "With it, make a grain offering every morning—one-sixth of an ephah, moistened with one-third hin of oil. That's a daily devotion. No excuses."
46.15: "The lamb, the grain, and the oil—all that? Every morning like clockwork. That's how you honor the Lord daily."
46.16: "Now if the prince wanna bless his sons with a piece of his inheritance? That's cool. It's theirs for keeps."
46.17: "But if he gifts land to a servant? That's a lease. It's theirs until the Year of Freedom. Then it goes back to the prince. His sons still keep their part though."
46.18: "And he better not be out here snatchin' other folks' land either. He gotta bless his own kids from his own stash. Ain't no pushing people out they homes."
46.19: Then he took me through this entrance on the side of the gate—led me into the priests' private area that faced north. There was a special spot at the far west end.
46.20: He told me, "This is the spot where priests cook up the guilt offerings and sin offerings. They also bake the grain here. They can't bring that food out to the outer court or else folks gon' get sanctified the wrong way."
46.21: Then he walked me through the outer court. We did a lap around the four corners, and each corner had its own little court.
46.22: Every corner court was forty cubits long, thirty cubits wide—all uniform, same measurements.
46.23: These spots had stone rows lining the edges. And under the stones? Fire pits—ready for cookin'.
46.24: And he said, "These here? These are the temple kitchens. The workers gon' boil and cook the people's sacrifices right here."

47.1: Then he took me back to the temple door—and look, water was flowin' from under the front entrance, headin' east. Since the temple faced east, the water came from under the right side of the temple, south of the altar.
47.2: He took me out through the north gate and brought me around to the east gate—and sure enough, water was pourin' out the right side.
47.3: Then the man stepped out eastward, measuring line in hand. He walked 1,000 cubits and had me walk through the water—it was up to my ankles.
47.4: He measured another 1,000, brought me through again—now it hit my knees. Measured another 1,000—it came up to my waist.
47.5: Another 1,000, and now the water was deep. Too deep to walk across. I'd have to swim—this was a full-blown river now.
47.6: He looked at me and said, 'Son of man, you peep this?' Then he walked me back to the riverbank.
47.7: When I got back, I saw trees—lots of 'em—growing on both sides of the river.
47.8: Then he said, 'This water flows down to the east, into the valley, and eventually into the sea. And when it hits the sea? The water in there gets healed.'
47.9: 'Every living thing that touches that river gon' live. A whole lotta fish gon' be in there too, 'cause them waters get healed. Wherever that river flows, life follows.'
47.10: 'Fishermen gon' set up from En Gedi to En Eglaim—nets stretched out everywhere. Fish gon' be just like the ones in the Mediterranean—plentiful, all kinds.'
47.11: 'But the swampy spots and the marshes? Nah, they won't get healed. They stay salty.'
47.12: 'But along both sides of that river? You gon' see trees that feed you. Leaves never fade. Fruit never stop. Every month, new fruit show up—'cause the water flowin' from the temple fuels 'em. The fruit gon' feed folks, and the leaves? They gon' be medicine.'
47.13: Then the Lord said: 'Here's how y'all gon' divide the land among the twelve tribes. Joseph? He get two portions.'
47.14: 'Y'all gon' get equal shares. I swore to your ancestors I'd give 'em this land—and now it's yours.'
47.15: Here's the north border: Start at the Mediterranean (Great Sea), go by Hethlon, to Zedad,
47.16: Then Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim (between Damascus and Hamath), then down to Hazar Hatticon, near Hauran.
47.17: From the sea to Hazar Enan, by Damascus' border, and into Hamath territory. That's your northern line.
47.18: East side? Run it from Hauran to Damascus, through Gilead, along the Jordan, to the eastern side of the Dead Sea.
47.19: South side? From Tamar to Meribah's waters near Kadesh, along the brook to the Great Sea.
47.20: West side? Straight down the Mediterranean, from the southern border up to the edge near Hamath.
47.21: 'That's the land. Divide it up among the tribes of Israel.'
47.22: 'And don't forget the foreigners who livin' among y'all and raising kids here—they count too. Treat 'em like native-born. They get inheritance just like everybody else.'
47.23: 'Wherever a foreigner settles—give them land in that tribe's portion. That's what I said,' says the Lord God.

48.1: Alright, here go the names of the tribes and how the land gon' be split. From the north border—startin' at that road to Hethlon, near Hamath, all the way to Hazar Enan by Damascus—you got Dan. They get land from east to west.
48.2: Right under Dan? Asher's portion, stretchin' east to west.
48.3: Under Asher? Naphtali, same setup—east to west.
48.4: Next up: Manasseh, east to west.
48.5: Then Ephraim's section, right below Manasseh, east to west.
48.6: Reuben follows, same line—east to west.
48.7: Then Judah gets theirs, from east to west too.
48.8: Now under Judah, we hit that special zone—the holy district. Same width as the others, 25,000 cubits long. This area got the sanctuary dead in the middle.
48.9: This sacred district you set aside for the Lord? It's 25,000 long, 10,000 wide.
48.10: This area go to the priests—the holy ones from Zadok's line. 25,000 cubits north and south, 10,000 east and west. God's sanctuary sit right in the middle.
48.11: These priests stayed true. They ain't fall off when Israel did. They held it down when the Levites didn't. So they get this holy ground.
48.12: Their land gon' be the holiest piece, right next to the Levites' section.
48.13: Levites get their own chunk—same size: 25,000 long, 10,000 wide.
48.14: And listen—they can't sell it, swap it, or give it away. That's the Lord's best, and it stays that way.
48.15: The leftover 5,000 in width next to the 25,000 length? That's city land—homes, open space, community life. City go in the center.
48.16: The city dimensions: 4,500 cubits north, south, east, and west.
48.17: Each side gets a buffer of 250 cubits of green space.
48.18: The rest of the land, 10,000 cubits east and west alongside the holy district, gon' be farmland to feed the city workers.
48.19: And the workers? They come from all the tribes of Israel. It's a community effort.
48.20: So the whole zone—holy district plus city space—is 25,000 by 25,000 cubits. One big square for the Lord and His people.
48.21: Everything else? That's for the prince—on both sides of the holy and city district. East to west, adjacent to the tribes. The sanctuary still at the heart of it all.
48.22: Between Judah and Benjamin's borders, the land belongs to the prince—outside the city and Levites' parts.
48.23: Now the rest of the tribes, from east to west—Benjamin's up first.
48.27: Then Gad's, stretchin' all the way down.
48.28: Gad's border reaches from Tamar to Meribah by Kadesh, down the brook to the Great Sea. That's the south end.
48.29: This the land y'all gon' divide by lot. These the official pieces each tribe gets, says the Lord God.
48.30: These the city exits. North side? 4,500 cubits long.
48.31: Three gates on the north: one for Reuben, one for Judah, one for Levi.
48.32: East side? 4,500 cubits. Gates for Joseph, Benjamin, and Dan.
48.33: South side? Same length. Gates for Simeon, Issachar, and Zebulun.
48.34: West side? 4,500 cubits. Gates for Gad, Asher, and Naphtali.
48.35: All around, the city perimeter? 18,000 cubits. And from that day forward, the city gon' be called—THE LORD IS THERE.
